            expect(callOrder).toEqual([
              'delLink:sales-orders-to-customer',
              'createLink:sales-orders-to-customer',
              'delEntry:sales.entities.supplier',
            ]);
            expect(updateLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'deletes and recreates an existing link when its link type ' +
              'changed even if endpoint references match',
          async () => {
            // Stage an existing `semantic-relationship` link whose
            // `entryReferences` already match the V1 `schema-join` link emitted
            // by `STAR_DOCS`. Because `entryLinkType` is immutable in Dataplex,
            // the link must still be deleted and recreated.
            const sameRefsWrongType = {
              ...linkEntry(
                  'sales-orders-to-customer',
                  ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']),
              entryLinkType:
                  'projects/dataplex-types/locations/global/entryLinkTypes/' +
                  'semantic-relationship',
            };
            const {createLink, updateLink, delLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([sameRefsWrongType]),
              createLink: () => ok({}),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(true);
            expect(result.linked).toBe(1);
            expect(delLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(delLink.mock.calls[0][3]).toBe('sales-orders-to-customer');
            expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(updateLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'updates an existing link in place without deleting when its ' +
              'endpoint references match',
          async () => {
            // Dataplex returns project numbers in server-side resource names,
            // whereas the emitted link carries the project ID ('dest').
            const matchingLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer'],
                '123456789');
            const {createLink, updateLink, delLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([matchingLink]),
              createLink: () => err(409, 'already exists'),
              updateLink: ok({}),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(true);
            expect(result.linked).toBe(1);
            expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(updateLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(delLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'a schema-join link whose references come back in the opposite ' +
              'order still matches and is updated in place',
          async () => {
            const reversedLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.customer', 'sales.entities.orders']);
            const {createLink, updateLink, delLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([reversedLink]),
              createLink: () => err(409, 'already exists'),
              updateLink: ok({}),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(true);
            expect(result.linked).toBe(1);
            expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(updateLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(delLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'a link that lookupEntryLinks does not return is updated in place',
          async () => {
            const {createLink, updateLink, delLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([]),
              createLink: () => err(409, 'already exists'),
              getLink: ok(gotLinkEntry(
                  'sales-orders-to-customer',
                  ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer'])),
              updateLink: ok({}),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(true);
            expect(result.linked).toBe(1);
            expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(updateLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
            expect(delLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'a 403 on updating a link the lookup returned reports the ' +
              'server\'s message and does not blame another link',
          async () => {
            // Dataplex also answers 403 to a caller that may not update the
            // link. The lookup shows the link exists, so no other link is
            // involved.
            const matchingLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer'],
                '123456789');
            stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([matchingLink]),
              createLink: () => err(409, 'already exists'),
              updateLink:
                  err(403, 'Permission denied on resource (or it may not exist)'),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Model \'sales\': entry link \'sales-orders-to-customer\': ' +
                    'Permission denied on resource (or it may not exist)');
          });

      test(
          'a 409 on creating the ID of a deleted stale link blames another ' +
              'link and says to push again',
          async () => {
            // The push deletes the stale link, so its ID has no link when the
            // create returns 409, and the read returns 404. Another link holds
            // the new endpoints.
            const staleLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([staleLink]),
              createLink: () => err(409, 'already exists'),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Model \'sales\': failed to create entry link ' +
                    '\'sales-orders-to-customer\' because another ' +
                    '\'schema-join\' link already connects ' +
                    '\'sales.entities.orders\' and \'sales.entities.customer\'; ' +
                    'Knowledge Catalog returned: already exists (push again to ' +
                    'restore the link)');
          });

      test(
          'a link with a reference outside the model is not deleted, and ' +
              'the push fails naming the link before any orphan is deleted',
          async () => {
            const foreignRefLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'other.entities.customer']);
            const orphan = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-supplier',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            const {createLink, updateLink, delLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([foreignRefLink, orphan]),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Model \'sales\': entry link \'sales-orders-to-customer\' ' +
                    'already exists and references entry ' +
                    '\'other.entities.customer\' outside this model; rename ' +
                    'the relationship or delete the existing link');
            expect(delLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
            expect(updateLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
            expect(createLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'returns an error when deleting a link with changed references fails',
          async () => {
            const staleDottedLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            const {createLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([staleDottedLink]),
              delLink: () => err(500, 'delete failed'),
            });

            const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(
                models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, {...OPTS, v2Aspects: true});

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Deleting stale entry link ' +
                    '\'sales-orders-to-customer\' from model \'sales\' ' +
                    'failed: delete failed');
            expect(createLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'a failed stale link delete after the delete of a renamed ' +
              'relationship\'s link says to push again',
          async () => {
            // `sales-old-orders-to-customer` joins the entities that the
            // emitted `sales-orders-to-customer` joins, so the push deletes it
            // to make way. The push then stops before writing the new link.
            const renamedFrom = linkEntry(
                'sales-old-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            const staleLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            const {createLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([renamedFrom, staleLink]),
              delLink: (id) => id === 'sales-orders-to-customer' ?
                  err(500, 'delete failed') :
                  ok({}),
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.unlinked).toBe(1);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Deleting stale entry link ' +
                    '\'sales-orders-to-customer\' from model \'sales\' ' +
                    'failed: delete failed (push again to restore the link)');
            expect(createLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
          });

      test(
          'a thrown error on a link delete after an earlier delete in the ' +
              'same batch names the link, keeps the count and says to push ' +
              'again',
          async () => {
            // The first orphan is a renamed relationship's old link, so its
            // delete leaves the pair without a link.
            const renamedFrom = linkEntry(
                'sales-old-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            const dropped = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-supplier',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([renamedFrom, dropped]),
              delLink: (id) => {
                if (id === 'sales-orders-to-supplier') {
                  throw new Error('socket hang up');
                }
                return ok({});
              },
            });

            const result =
                await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.unlinked).toBe(1);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Deleting orphaned entry link ' +
                    '\'sales-orders-to-supplier\' from model \'sales\' ' +
                    'failed: socket hang up (push again to restore the link)');
          });

      test(
          'returns an error when recreating a link after deletion fails',
          async () => {
            const staleDottedLink = linkEntry(
                'sales-orders-to-customer',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([staleDottedLink]),
              delLink: () => err(404, 'already gone'),
              createLink: () => err(500, 'recreate failed'),
            });

            const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(
                models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, {...OPTS, v2Aspects: true});

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe(
                    'Model \'sales\': entry link ' +
                    '\'sales-orders-to-customer\': recreate failed ' +
                    '(push again to restore the link)');
          });

      test(
          'an error on one link after another replaced a deleted link has ' +
              'no push-again hint',
          async () => {
            // `sales-old-a` joins the pair `sales-a` takes, and `sales-a` is
            // written. The update of `sales-b` fails, and that link still
            // exists.
            const linkA = linkEntry(
                'sales-a', ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            const linkB = linkEntry(
                'sales-b', ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([
                linkEntry(
                    'sales-old-a',
                    ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']),
                linkB,
              ]),
              createLink: (id) =>
                  id === 'sales-b' ? err(409, 'already exists') : ok({}),
              updateLink: err(500, 'backend error'),
            });
            const emitted: EmittedModel[] = [{
              model: 'sales',
              resources: {
                entries: [{name: entryName('sales'), entryType: MODEL_TYPE}],
                entryLinks: [linkA, linkB],
                ownedPrefixes: ['sales.entities.'],
                warnings: [],
              },
            }];

            const result = await deployEmittedModels(emitted, [], CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(false);
            expect(result.details)
                .toBe('Model \'sales\': entry link \'sales-b\': backend error');
          });

      test(
          'two relationships that swap entity pairs have both stale links ' +
              'deleted before either new link is created',
          async () => {
            const swapDoc = `
version: "0.2.0.dev0"
semantic_model:
  - name: sales
    datasets:
      - name: orders
        source: demo.sales.orders
        primary_key: [o_orderkey]
        fields:
          - name: o_orderkey
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: o_orderkey }]
          - name: o_custkey
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: o_custkey }]
          - name: o_suppkey
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: o_suppkey }]
      - name: customer
        source: demo.sales.customer
        primary_key: [c_custkey]
        fields:
          - name: c_custkey
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: c_custkey }]
      - name: supplier
        source: demo.sales.supplier
        primary_key: [s_suppkey]
        fields:
          - name: s_suppkey
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: s_suppkey }]
    relationships:
      - name: rel_a
        from: orders
        to: customer
        from_columns: [o_custkey]
        to_columns: [c_custkey]
      - name: rel_b
        from: orders
        to: supplier
        from_columns: [o_suppkey]
        to_columns: [s_suppkey]
`;
            // Previously, `rel_a` connected orders <-> supplier and `rel_b`
            // connected orders <-> customer (the opposite pairs).
            const oldRelA = linkEntry(
                'sales-rel-a',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.supplier']);
            const oldRelB = linkEntry(
                'sales-rel-b',
                ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
            const callOrder: string[] = [];
            const {createLink, delLink, updateLink} = stubClient({
              existing: [
                {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
                {id: 'sales.entities.supplier', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
              ],
              links: () => ok([oldRelA, oldRelB]),
              delLink: (id) => {
                callOrder.push(`delLink:${id}`);
                return ok({});
              },
              createLink: (id) => {
                callOrder.push(`createLink:${id}`);
                return ok({});
              },
            });

            const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(
                models([{name: 'swap.yaml', text: swapDoc}]), CTX, OPTS);

            expect(result.success).toBe(true);
            expect(result.linked).toBe(2);
            expect(result.unlinked).toBe(0);
            expect(delLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
            expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
            expect(updateLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
            expect(callOrder).toEqual([
              'delLink:sales-rel-a',
              'delLink:sales-rel-b',
              'createLink:sales-rel-a',
              'createLink:sales-rel-b',
            ]);
          });
    });


describe('deployKnowledgeCatalog: both relationship link types', () => {
  // The STAR model's anchor and entity entries, as a re-push finds them.
  const STAR_ENTITY_ENTRIES = [
    {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
    {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
    {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
  ];
  const SEMANTIC_REL_LINK_TYPE =
      'projects/dataplex-types/locations/global/entryLinkTypes/' +
      'semantic-relationship';

  test(
      'lookupEntryLinks omits entryLinkTypes and filters to schema-join and ' +
          'semantic-relationship links',
      async () => {
        // Stage one orphaned `schema-join` link, one orphaned
        // `semantic-relationship` link, and one non-relationship `synonym`
        // link on the model's entities.
        const orphanSchemaJoin = linkEntry(
            'sales-old-join',
            ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
        const orphanSemanticRel = {
          ...linkEntry(
              'sales-old-rel',
              ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']),
          entryLinkType: SEMANTIC_REL_LINK_TYPE,
        };
        const unrelatedLink = {
          ...linkEntry(
              'sales-synonym-link',
              ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']),
          entryLinkType:
              'projects/dataplex-types/locations/global/entryLinkTypes/synonym',
        };
        const {lookupLinks, delLink} = stubClient({
          existing: [
            {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
          ],
          links: (entry: string) => entry.endsWith('sales.entities.orders') ?
              ok([orphanSchemaJoin, orphanSemanticRel, unrelatedLink]) :
              ok([]),
        });

        const result =
            await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

        // `lookupEntryLinks` omitted `entryLinkTypes` and only the two
        // relationship orphans were deleted.
        expect(result.success).toBe(true);
        expect(result.unlinked).toBe(2);
        expect(lookupLinks.mock.calls.map(c => c[2])).toEqual([
          {entry: entryName('sales.entities.orders')},
          {entry: entryName('sales.entities.customer')},
        ]);
        expect(delLink.mock.calls.map(c => c[3]).sort()).toEqual([
          'sales-old-join',
          'sales-old-rel',
        ]);
      });

  test(
      'looks up links only through entity entries, skipping model and ' +
          'metric entries',
      async () => {
        const {lookupLinks} = stubClient({
          existing: [
            {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.metrics.total_revenue', type: METRIC_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.metrics.order_count', type: METRIC_TYPE},
          ],
        });

        const result =
            await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

        expect(result.success).toBe(true);
        expect(lookupLinks.mock.calls.map(c => c[2])).toEqual([
          {entry: entryName('sales.entities.orders')},
          {entry: entryName('sales.entities.customer')},
        ]);
      });

  test(
      'lookupEntryLinks skips relationship links stored in a sibling entry ' +
          'group',
      async () => {
        // A relationship link created in a sibling entry group (`other-eg`)
        // that references this model's entities must not shadow the model's
        // own link on update or be treated as an orphan to delete in `eg`.
        const siblingSameIdLink = {
          ...linkEntry(
              'sales-orders-to-customer',
              ['sales.entities.orders', 'other.entities.external']),
          name: 'projects/123456789/locations/us/entryGroups/other-eg/' +
              'entryLinks/sales-orders-to-customer',
          entryReferences: [
            {
              name: entryName('sales.entities.orders', '123456789'),
              type: 'UNSPECIFIED',
            },
            {
              name: 'projects/123456789/locations/us/entryGroups/other-eg/' +
                  'entries/other.entities.external',
              type: 'UNSPECIFIED',
            },
          ],
        };
        const siblingOrphanCandidate = {
          ...linkEntry(
              'sales-sibling-link',
              ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']),

describe('deployKnowledgeCatalog: a relationship from an entity to itself', () => {
  // `manager` and `mentor` join `employee` to itself. `assignment` joins
  // `employee` to `department` and publishes the link `hr-assignment`.
  const SELF_DOCS = [{
    name: 'hr.yaml',
    text: `
version: "0.2.0.dev0"
semantic_model:
  - name: hr
    datasets:
      - name: employee
        source: demo.hr.employee
        primary_key: [employee_id]
        fields:
          - name: employee_id
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: employee_id }]
          - name: manager_id
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: manager_id }]
          - name: mentor_id
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: mentor_id }]
          - name: department_id
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: department_id }]
      - name: department
        source: demo.hr.department
        primary_key: [department_id]
        fields:
          - name: department_id
            expression:
              dialects: [{ dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: department_id }]
    relationships:
      - name: manager
        from: employee
        to: employee
        from_columns: [manager_id]
        to_columns: [employee_id]
      - name: mentor
        from: employee
        to: employee
        from_columns: [mentor_id]
        to_columns: [employee_id]
      - name: assignment
        from: employee
        to: department
        from_columns: [department_id]
        to_columns: [department_id]
`,
  }];

  const SELF_WARNINGS = [
    '[hr] relationship \'manager\': skipped because Knowledge Catalog does ' +
        'not support a relationship from an entity to itself.',
    '[hr] relationship \'mentor\': skipped because Knowledge Catalog does ' +
        'not support a relationship from an entity to itself.',
  ];

  test('validateOnly warns about each one and plans no link for it',
       async () => {
         const {list, create, createLink} = stubClient();

         const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(
             models(SELF_DOCS), CTX, {...OPTS, validateOnly: true});

         expect(result.success).toBe(true);
         expect(result.warnings).toEqual(SELF_WARNINGS);
         expect(result.plan).toContain('  1 schema-join link:');
         expect(result.plan).toContain('    - hr-assignment');
         expect(list).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
         expect(create).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
         expect(createLink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
       });

  test('a push skips it and writes every other link', async () => {
    const {createLink} = stubClient();

    const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(SELF_DOCS), CTX, OPTS);

    expect(result.success).toBe(true);
    expect(result.warnings).toEqual(SELF_WARNINGS);
    expect(result.linked).toBe(1);
    expect(createLink.mock.calls.map(c => c[3])).toEqual(['hr-assignment']);
  });

  test('a push passes the warnings to onWarnings before the first write',
       async () => {
         const events: string[] = [];
         stubClient({
           create: (id) => {
             events.push(`create:${id}`);
             return ok({});
           },
         });

         const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(models(SELF_DOCS), CTX, {
           ...OPTS,
           onWarnings: (warnings) => events.push(...warnings),
         });

         expect(result.success).toBe(true);
         expect(events.slice(0, 3)).toEqual([...SELF_WARNINGS, 'create:hr']);
       });

  test('deployEmittedModels also passes them before the first write',
       async () => {
         const events: string[] = [];
         stubClient({create: (id) => (events.push(`create:${id}`), ok({}))});
         const resources = {
           entries: [{name: entryName('hr'), entryType: MODEL_TYPE}],
           entryLinks: [], ownedPrefixes: ['hr.'], warnings: [],
         };

         const result = await deployEmittedModels(
             [{model: 'hr', resources}], ['a warning'], CTX,
             {...OPTS, onWarnings: (warnings) => events.push(...warnings)});

         expect(result.success).toBe(true);
         expect(events).toEqual(['a warning', 'create:hr']);
       });
});


describe('deployKnowledgeCatalog: cross-layout V1 -> V2 cleanup', () => {
  test(
      'pushing with v2Aspects: true into an entry group holding V1 entries ' +
          'and schema-join links creates V2 entries and links and deletes ' +
          'old V1 entries and links',
      async () => {
        // The entry group holds V1 dotted entries (`sales`,
        // `sales.entities.orders`, `sales.entities.customer`,
        // `sales.metrics.total_revenue`, `sales.metrics.order_count`), a
        // `schema-join` link whose ID collides with the V2 relationship link
        // (`sales-orders-to-customer`), and an orphaned `schema-join` link
        // whose ID is no longer emitted (`sales-orders-to-supplier`).
        const collidingV1Link = linkEntry(
            'sales-orders-to-customer',
            ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
        const orphanV1Link = linkEntry(
            'sales-orders-to-supplier',
            ['sales.entities.orders', 'sales.entities.customer']);
        const {create, update, del, createLink, delLink} = stubClient({
          existing: [
            {id: 'sales', type: MODEL_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.orders', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.entities.customer', type: ENTITY_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.metrics.total_revenue', type: METRIC_TYPE},
            {id: 'sales.metrics.order_count', type: METRIC_TYPE},
          ],
          create: (id) => id === 'sales' ? err(409, 'already exists') : ok({}),
          links: (entry: string) => entry.endsWith('sales.entities.orders') ?
              ok([collidingV1Link, orphanV1Link]) :
              ok([]),
          createLink: () => ok({}),
        });

        const result = await deployKnowledgeCatalog(
            models(STAR_DOCS), CTX, {...OPTS, v2Aspects: true});

        expect(result.success).toBe(true);
        expect(result.updated).toBe(1);  // anchor 'sales'
        expect(result.created).toBe(4);  // 2 slash entities + 2 slash metrics
        expect(result.linked)
            .toBe(1);  // relationship link recreated with V2 slash endpoints
        expect(result.deleted).toBe(4);   // 4 old dotted entries deleted
        expect(result.unlinked).toBe(1);  // orphan V1 schema-join link deleted
        expect(update).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        expect(createLink).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        expect(create.mock.calls.map(c => c[3]).sort()).toEqual([
          'sales',
          'sales/entities/customer',
          'sales/entities/orders',
          'sales/metrics/order_count',
          'sales/metrics/total_revenue',
        ]);
        expect(del.mock.calls.map(c => c[3]).sort()).toEqual([
          'sales.entities.customer',
          'sales.entities.orders',
          'sales.metrics.order_count',
          'sales.metrics.total_revenue',
        ]);
        expect(delLink.mock.calls.map(c => c[3]).sort()).toEqual([
          'sales-orders-to-customer',
          'sales-orders-to-supplier',
        ]);
      });
});

// Tests for the semantic-model Spanner deploy leg
// (src/libts/semantic/deploy_spanner.ts).
//
// `spannerGraphTargets` is exercised as a pure function; `deploySpanner` is
// exercised end to end over a fixture (loader -> IR -> generator -> target),
// with the Spanner client stubbed so no network call is made.

import {describe, expect, spyOn, test} from 'bun:test';
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';

import {ApiContext} from '../../../src/libts/gcp/context';
import * as spannerClient from '../../../src/libts/gcp/spanner';
import {deploySpanner} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/deploy_spanner';
import {spannerGraphTargets} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/deployment_target';
import {SemanticModel} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';
import {loadSemanticModels} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/loader';

const CTX = new ApiContext('test-project', 'us', 'test-token');

function models(
    docs: {name: string; text: string}[], defaultProject = 'test-project') {
  const r = loadSemanticModels(
      docs, {defaultProject, allowLegacyBareSource: true});
  if (r.error) throw new Error(r.error);
  return r.models;
}

const FIXTURES = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures');

const SPANNER_URI =
    '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/demo/instances/prod/databases/commerce/propertyGraphs/sales_graph';
const BQ_URI =
    '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/demo/datasets/sales/propertyGraphs/sales_graph';

const OSSIE = fs.readFileSync(
    path.join(FIXTURES, 'sales_spanner_graph_target.yaml'), 'utf8');

function modelWithExtension(data: string, vendor = 'GOOGLE'): SemanticModel {
  return {
    name: 'm',
    entities: [],
    relationships: [],
    metrics: [],
    customExtensions: [{vendorName: vendor, data}],
  };
}


describe('spannerGraphTargets', () => {
  test('parses a Spanner Graph deployment target', () => {
    const {targets, malformed} = spannerGraphTargets(
        modelWithExtension(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [SPANNER_URI]})));
    expect(targets).toEqual([
      {
        project: 'demo',
        instance: 'prod',
        database: 'commerce',
        graphName: 'sales_graph',
        uri: SPANNER_URI,
      },
    ]);
    expect(malformed).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('a BigQuery target is not a Spanner target, and not malformed', () => {
    // A BigQuery URI is a recognized destination, just not a Spanner one, so it
    // is neither returned as a Spanner target nor flagged as a typo.
    const {targets, malformed} = spannerGraphTargets(
        modelWithExtension(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [BQ_URI]})));
    expect(targets).toEqual([]);
    expect(malformed).toEqual([]);
  });

  // Same for the other recognized destination. An AlloyDB target is a store to
  // run against rather than a graph to deploy, so the Spanner leg passes over
  // it -- and it is not a typo, so it must not be reported as one either.
  test('an AlloyDB target is not a Spanner target, and not malformed', () => {
    const pg =
        '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/instances/i/databases/d';
    const {targets, malformed} = spannerGraphTargets(
        modelWithExtension(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [pg]})));
    expect(targets).toEqual([]);
    expect(malformed).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('an unsupported URI is collected as malformed', () => {
    const bad = '//cloudsql.googleapis.com/projects/p/whatever';
    const {targets, malformed} = spannerGraphTargets(
        modelWithExtension(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [bad]})));
    expect(targets).toEqual([]);
    expect(malformed).toEqual([bad]);
  });

  test('rejects a graph name with an injection character', () => {
    const evil =
        '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/demo/instances/prod/databases/commerce/propertyGraphs/g`;DROP';
    const {targets, malformed} = spannerGraphTargets(
        modelWithExtension(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [evil]})));
    expect(targets).toEqual([]);
    expect(malformed).toEqual([evil]);
  });
});


describe('deploySpanner', () => {
  test('validateOnly returns the DDL without calling Spanner', async () => {
    const ddlSpy =
        spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'updateDatabaseDdl');
    try {
      const res = await deploySpanner(
          models([{name: 'sales', text: OSSIE}]), CTX, {validateOnly: true});
      expect(res.success).toBe(true);
      expect(res.deployed).toBe(0);
      expect(ddlSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

      const ddl = res.ddl.join('\n');
      expect(ddl).toContain('CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH sales_graph');
      // Bare table name, not the three-part BigQuery source.
      expect(ddl).toContain('Orders AS orders');
      // The metric is dropped (Spanner has no MEASURE).
      expect(res.warnings.some(w => w.includes('total_revenue'))).toBe(true);
    } finally {
      ddlSpy.mockRestore();
    }
  });

  test(
      'applies the DDL to the target database and polls to completion',
      async () => {
        const ddlSpy =
            spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'updateDatabaseDdl')
                .mockImplementation(async () => ({
                                      status: 200,
                                      result: {name: 'op-1', done: false},
                                    }));
        const opSpy =
            spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'getOperation')
                .mockImplementation(
                    async () => ({status: 200, result: {done: true}}));
        try {
          const res = await deploySpanner(
              models([{name: 'sales', text: OSSIE}]), CTX, {pollBackoffMs: 0});
          expect(res.success).toBe(true);
          expect(res.deployed).toBe(1);
          expect(ddlSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

          // updateDatabaseDdl(project, instance, database, statements) -- the
          // coords come from the deployment-target URI.
          const [project, instance, database, statements] =
              ddlSpy.mock.calls[0];
          expect(project).toBe('demo');
          expect(instance).toBe('prod');
          expect(database).toBe('commerce');
          expect(statements[0])
              .toContain('CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH sales_graph');
          // Spanner's updateDatabaseDdl rejects a statement ending in ';'
          // (verified live); the leg strips the generator's trailing semicolon
          // for the wire, but the returned/printed DDL keeps it for
          // readability.
          expect(statements[0].trimEnd().endsWith(';')).toBe(false);
          expect(res.ddl[0].trimEnd().endsWith(';')).toBe(true);

          // The returned operation was polled by name until done.
          expect(opSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
          expect(opSpy.mock.calls[0][0]).toBe('op-1');
        } finally {
          ddlSpy.mockRestore();
          opSpy.mockRestore();
        }
      });

  test('a completed operation carrying an error fails the deploy', async () => {
    const ddlSpy =
        spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'updateDatabaseDdl')
            .mockImplementation(async () => ({
                                  status: 200,
                                  result: {
                                    name: 'op-1',
                                    done: true,
                                    error: {code: 3, message: 'bad DDL'},
                                  },
                                }));
    try {
      const res = await deploySpanner(
          models([{name: 'sales', text: OSSIE}]), CTX, {pollBackoffMs: 0});
      expect(res.success).toBe(false);
      expect(res.details).toContain('bad DDL');
      expect(res.deployed).toBe(0);
    } finally {
      ddlSpy.mockRestore();
    }
  });

  test(
      'an operation that never completes fails after exhausting polls',
      async () => {
        const ddlSpy =
            spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'updateDatabaseDdl')
                .mockImplementation(async () => ({
                                      status: 200,
                                      result: {name: 'op-1', done: false},
                                    }));
        const opSpy =
            spyOn(spannerClient.SpannerClient.prototype, 'getOperation')
                .mockImplementation(
                    async () => ({status: 200, result: {done: false}}));
        try {
          const res = await deploySpanner(
              models([{name: 'sales', text: OSSIE}]), CTX,
              {pollBackoffMs: 0, maxOperationPolls: 3});
          expect(res.success).toBe(false);
          expect(res.details).toContain('did not complete after 3 polls');
        } finally {
          ddlSpy.mockRestore();
          opSpy.mockRestore();
        }
      });

  test('a model with no Spanner target fails clearly', async () => {
    // A BigQuery-only model handed to the Spanner leg has nothing to deploy;
    // commands.ts routes such models away, so this is the direct-call guard.
    const bqDoc = fs.readFileSync(
        path.join(FIXTURES, 'sales_bq_graph_target.yaml'), 'utf8');
    const res = await deploySpanner(
        models([{name: 'sales', text: bqDoc}]), CTX, {validateOnly: true});
    expect(res.success).toBe(false);
    expect(res.details).toContain('no Spanner Graph deploymentTarget');
  });
});

// Tests for reading a model's named deployments (deployment_target.ts): the
// `--deployment` selection, resolving each entry's target to its engine and
// coordinates, and googleDeploymentTargets reading the list instead of the
// GOOGLE block the loader folds it into.

import {describe, expect, test} from 'bun:test';

import {destinationKey, googleDeploymentTargets, parseDeploymentSelection, resolveModelDeployments} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/deployment_target';
import {SemanticModel} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';
import {loadModels} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/loader';

const BQ_URI =
    '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme/datasets/sales/propertyGraphs/retail';
const SPANNER_URI =
    '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/acme/instances/ops/databases/sales/propertyGraphs/retail';
const ALLOY_URI =
    '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/acme/locations/us-central1/clusters/main/databases/sales';
const ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI =
    '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/acme/locations/us-central1/clusters/main/instances/primary/databases/sales';

// A Google-flavor model loaded from `deployments:` entries, so it carries the
// GOOGLE block the loader folds the targets into.
function modelWith(
    deployments: Array<{name: string; target: string; profile?: string}>):
    SemanticModel {
  const entries = deployments.map(
      d => `      - name: ${d.name}\n        target: "${d.target}"\n` +
          (d.profile ? `        profile: ${d.profile}\n` : ''));
  const text = `version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: retail
    deployments:
${entries.join('')}    entities:
      - name: Order
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - { name: id }
`;
  return loadModels(text, {bindingOptional: true}).models[0];
}

function resolved(model: SemanticModel, selected?: string[]) {
  const res = resolveModelDeployments(model, selected);
  if ('error' in res) throw new Error(res.error);
  return res.deployments;
}

function errorOf(model: SemanticModel, selected?: string[]): string {
  const res = resolveModelDeployments(model, selected);
  if (!('error' in res)) throw new Error('expected an error');
  return res.error;
}


describe('parseDeploymentSelection', () => {
  test('a single name', () => {
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection('a')).toEqual(['a']);
  });

  test('a comma-separated list', () => {
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection('a,b')).toEqual(['a', 'b']);
  });

  test('a repeated flag, keeping the first of each name', () => {
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection(['a,b', 'c', 'a'])).toEqual(['a', 'b', 'c']);
  });

  test('pieces are trimmed and empty ones dropped', () => {
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection(' a , ,b ')).toEqual(['a', 'b']);
  });

  test('an absent or negated flag selects nothing', () => {
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection(true)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection(false)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(parseDeploymentSelection(undefined)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  // A repeated flag fails when any one occurrence names nothing. A bare
  // `--deployment` among repeated ones arrives as `true`.
  test('a flag that names no deployment is an error', () => {
    for (const raw of
             ['', ',', [' , ', ''], ['a', ''], ['a', ' , '], ['a', true], []]) {
      expect(() => parseDeploymentSelection(raw))
          .toThrow('--deployment names no deployment');
    }
  });
});


describe('resolveModelDeployments: resource URIs', () => {
  test('a BigQuery graph', () => {
    const [d] = resolved(modelWith([{name: 'bq_prod', target: BQ_URI}]));
    expect(d.engine).toBe('bigquery');
    expect(d.coordinates).toEqual(
        {project: 'acme', dataset: 'sales', graphName: 'retail', uri: BQ_URI});
  });

  test('a Spanner graph', () => {
    const [d] =
        resolved(modelWith([{name: 'spanner_prod', target: SPANNER_URI}]));
    expect(d.engine).toBe('spanner');
    expect(d.coordinates).toEqual({
      project: 'acme',
      instance: 'ops',
      database: 'sales',
      graphName: 'retail',
      uri: SPANNER_URI,
    });
  });

  test('an AlloyDB database, named by its cluster', () => {
    const [d] = resolved(modelWith([{name: 'alloy_prod', target: ALLOY_URI}]));
    expect(d.engine).toBe('alloydb');
    expect(d.coordinates).toEqual({
      project: 'acme',
      location: 'us-central1',
      cluster: 'main',
      database: 'sales',
      uri: ALLOY_URI,
    });
  });

  test('the instance-based AlloyDB URI is rejected', () => {
    const error =
        errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'alloy_prod', target: ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI}]));
    expect(error).toContain(
        `Model 'retail': deployment 'alloy_prod' targets '${
            ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI}', the instance-based AlloyDB URI, which ` +
        'names no real resource');
    expect(error).toContain(`write '${ALLOY_URI}'.`);
  });

  test('a URI of no supported destination is rejected', () => {
    const target =
        '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme/datasets/sales/tables/orders';
    expect(errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'bq_prod', target}])))
        .toContain(
            `deployment 'bq_prod' targets '${target}', which is not a ` +
            'BigQuery graph, a Spanner graph or an AlloyDB database');
  });
});


// A target may be written as its GCP resource name: the resource
// URI without the leading `//`. It parses to the same engine and coordinates,
// and `uri` keeps the form the author wrote, which is what pull returns.
describe('resolveModelDeployments: GCP resource names', () => {
  for (const [label, uri] of [
         ['BigQuery graph', BQ_URI],
         ['Spanner graph', SPANNER_URI],
         ['AlloyDB database', ALLOY_URI],
       ]) {
    test(`a ${label} written as a resource name parses like its URI`, () => {
      const name = uri.slice(2);
      const [fromName] = resolved(modelWith([{name: 'prod', target: name}]));
      const [fromUri] = resolved(modelWith([{name: 'prod', target: uri}]));
      expect(fromName.engine).toBe(fromUri.engine);
      expect(fromName.coordinates).toEqual({...fromUri.coordinates, uri: name});
    });
  }

  test('the instance-based AlloyDB resource name gets the same message', () => {
    const name = ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI.slice(2);
    const error = errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'alloy_prod', target: name}]));
    expect(error).toContain('the instance-based AlloyDB URI');
    expect(error).toContain(`write '${ALLOY_URI}'.`);
  });

  test('a resource name of no supported destination is rejected', () => {
    const target =
        'bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme/datasets/sales/tables/orders';
    expect(errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'bq_prod', target}])))
        .toContain(
            `deployment 'bq_prod' targets '${target}', which is not a ` +
            'BigQuery graph, a Spanner graph or an AlloyDB database');
  });

  test('a resource name and its URI are the same target', () => {
    expect(() => modelWith([
      {name: 'a', target: BQ_URI},
      {name: 'b', target: BQ_URI.slice(2)},
    ])).toThrow(
        `deployments 'a' and 'b' target the same resource '${
            BQ_URI.slice(2)}'`);
  });
});


// kcmd accepts no Knowledge Catalog name as a target, and the error names the
// resource URI form to write.
describe('resolveModelDeployments: Knowledge Catalog names', () => {
  const BQ_FORM =
      '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/datasets/<d>/propertyGraphs/<g>';

  test('a graph or database name is rejected with the URI form to write', () => {
    for (const [target, form] of [
           ['bigquery:graph:acme.sales.retail', BQ_FORM],
           ['bigquery:propertygraph:acme.sales.retail', BQ_FORM],
           [
             'spanner:graph:acme.regional-us-central1.ops.sales.retail',
             '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/instances/<i>/databases/<db>/propertyGraphs/<g>',
           ],
           [
             'alloydb:acme.us-central1.main.sales',
             '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/locations/<l>/clusters/<c>/databases/<db>',
           ],
         ]) {
      expect(errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'prod', target}])))
          .toBe(
              `Model 'retail': deployment 'prod' targets '${target}', which ` +
              `is a Knowledge Catalog name. Write the resource URI instead: ` +
              `'${form}'.`);
    }
  });

  test('any other catalog name gets every URI form', () => {
    const target = 'bigquery:acme.sales.retail';
    const error = errorOf(modelWith([{name: 'bq_prod', target}]));
    expect(error).toContain(
        `targets '${target}', which is not a BigQuery graph, a Spanner graph ` +
        'or an AlloyDB database. Write a resource URI:');
    expect(error).toContain(`'${BQ_FORM}'`);
  });
});


describe('destinationKey', () => {
  test('is the resource URI of a target written as one', () => {
    expect(destinationKey(BQ_URI)).toBe(BQ_URI);
    expect(destinationKey(SPANNER_URI)).toBe(SPANNER_URI);
    expect(destinationKey(ALLOY_URI)).toBe(ALLOY_URI);
    expect(destinationKey('not a target')).toBe('not a target');

  test('names a legacy AlloyDB database by its cluster-based URI', () => {
    expect(destinationKey(ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI)).toBe(ALLOY_URI);

  test('is the same for a resource name and its URI', () => {
    expect(destinationKey(BQ_URI.slice(2))).toBe(BQ_URI);
    expect(destinationKey(ALLOY_URI.slice(2))).toBe(ALLOY_URI);
    expect(destinationKey(ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI.slice(2))).toBe(ALLOY_URI);
  });

describe('resolveModelDeployments: profiles and selection', () => {
  const model = modelWith([

describe('googleDeploymentTargets reads the named list', () => {
  test('three deployments give three targets, not six', () => {
    const model = modelWith([
      {name: 'bq_prod', target: BQ_URI},
      {name: 'spanner_prod', target: SPANNER_URI},
      {name: 'alloy_prod', target: ALLOY_URI},
    ]);
    // The loader also folds the three targets into a GOOGLE block.
    expect(JSON.parse(model.customExtensions![0].data).deploymentTargets)
        .toEqual([BQ_URI, SPANNER_URI, ALLOY_URI]);
    const targets = googleDeploymentTargets(model);
    expect(targets.uris).toEqual([BQ_URI, SPANNER_URI, ALLOY_URI]);
    expect(targets.bigQuery).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(targets.spanner).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(targets.alloyDb).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(targets.malformed).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('a narrowed model sees only the deployments it keeps', () => {
    const model = modelWith([
      {name: 'bq_prod', target: BQ_URI},
      {name: 'spanner_prod', target: SPANNER_URI},
    ]);
    const narrowed = {...model, deployments: [model.deployments![1]]};
    expect(googleDeploymentTargets(narrowed).uris).toEqual([SPANNER_URI]);
  });

  test('a catalog name is malformed, in a list or in a GOOGLE block', () => {
    const target = 'bigquery:graph:acme.sales.retail';
    const listed = googleDeploymentTargets(
        modelWith([{name: 'bq_prod', target}]));
    expect(listed.bigQuery).toEqual([]);
    expect(listed.malformed).toEqual([target]);
    const vanilla = googleDeploymentTargets({
      name: 'm',
      entities: [],
      relationships: [],
      metrics: [],
      customExtensions: [{
        vendorName: 'GOOGLE',
        data: JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [target]}),
      }],
    });
    expect(vanilla.bigQuery).toEqual([]);
    expect(vanilla.malformed).toEqual([target]);
  });

  // A legacy file's `deployment_target:` may still hold the instance-based
  // URI, and keeps working until the demo moves off it.
  test('a legacy deployment_target keeps its instance-based AlloyDB URI', () => {
    const model = loadModels(
                      `version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: retail
    deployment_target: ${ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI}
    entities:
      - name: Order
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - { name: id }
`,
                      {bindingOptional: true, allowLegacyBareSource: true})
                      .models[0];
    expect(googleDeploymentTargets(model).alloyDb).toEqual([{
      project: 'acme',
      location: 'us-central1',
      cluster: 'main',
      instance: 'primary',
      database: 'sales',
      uri: ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI,
    }]);

    // Written as a resource name, it parses the same and keeps its spelling.
    const name = ALLOY_INSTANCE_URI.slice(2);
    const fromName = loadModels(
                         `version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: retail
    deployment_target: ${name}
    entities:
      - name: Order
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - { name: id }
`,
                         {bindingOptional: true, allowLegacyBareSource: true})
                         .models[0];
    expect(googleDeploymentTargets(fromName).alloyDb)
        .toEqual([{...googleDeploymentTargets(model).alloyDb[0], uri: name}]);
  });
});

// Behavior specification for the shared GoogleSQL property-graph generator
// (src/libts/semantic/graph_ddl.ts).
//
// The BigQuery goldens (`bigquery.e2e.test.ts`, `bigquery.test.ts`) pin the
// BigQuery engine's output. This file checks the shared code itself: that each
// of the four engine differences -- names, measures, element metadata, SQL
// text -- comes from the engine.
//

import {describe, expect, test} from 'bun:test';

import {generateGraphDdl, GraphEngine} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/graph_ddl';
import {fieldBinding, SemanticModel} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';


describe('each engine difference comes from the engine', () => {
  // Every hook writes a visible marker, so the expected DDL shows where the
  // shared code puts what each one returns.
  const MARKED: GraphEngine = {
    name: 'Marked',
    table: dataSource => `<table ${dataSource}>`,
    graphName: model => `<graph ${model.name}>`,
    placeMetrics: metrics => new Map([[
      'orders', ['<derived>', ...metrics.map(m => `<measure ${m.name}>`)]
    ]]),
    elementOptions: description =>
        description === undefined ? undefined : `<options ${description}>`,
    fieldOptions: field => field.description === undefined ?
        undefined :
        `<field options ${field.description}>`,
    // Other SQL than the field's own for the key column and `amount`, and none
    // for `notes`, so the expected DDL shows every place the graph reads a
    // field's SQL: properties, key and join columns, and the filter that leaves
    // out a field the engine has no SQL for.
    fieldExpression: field => {
      switch (field.name) {
        case 'order_id':
          return 'id';
        case 'amount':
          return 'amount_usd';
        case 'notes':
          return undefined;
        default:
          return fieldBinding(field);
      }
    },
    dialect: 'POSTGRES',
  };

  const MODEL: SemanticModel = {
    name: 'shop',
    entities: [
      {
        name: 'orders',
        dataSource: 'p.d.orders',
        keys: ['order_id'],
        description: 'One row per order',
        fields: [
          {name: 'order_id', expression: 'orders.order_id'},
          {name: 'amount', expression: 'orders.amount', description: 'Total'},
          {name: 'customer_id', expression: 'orders.customer_id'},
          {name: 'notes', expression: 'orders.notes'},
          {name: 'memo'},
        ],
      },
      {
        name: 'customers',
        dataSource: 'p.d.customers',
        keys: ['customer_id'],
        fields: [
          {name: 'customer_id', expression: 'CAST(customers.id AS STRING)'},
        ],
      },
    ],
    relationships: [
      {
        name: 'placed_by',
        source: {entity: 'orders', columns: ['customer_id']},
        destination: {entity: 'customers', columns: ['customer_id']},
        description: 'Who placed it',
      },
      {
        name: 'gifted_to',
        source: {entity: 'orders', columns: []},
        destination: {entity: 'customers', columns: []},
        description: 'Who received it',
        association: {
          dataSource: 'p.d.gifts',
          keys: ['gift_id'],
          sourceColumns: ['order_id'],
          destinationColumns: ['customer_id'],
          fields: [{
            name: 'message',
            expression: 'gifted_to.card_text',
            description: 'Card text',
          }],
        },
      },
      {
        name: 'from_ghost',
        source: {entity: 'ghost', columns: ['customer_id']},
        destination: {entity: 'customers', columns: ['customer_id']},
      },
    ],
    metrics: [{name: 'revenue', expression: 'SUM(orders.amount)'}],
    actions: [{name: 'refund', parameters: []}],
    constraints: [{name: 'amount_is_positive'}],
  };

  test('names, measures, metadata and SQL text land where the graph puts them',
       () => {
         expect(generateGraphDdl(MODEL, MARKED).ddl).toBe(`\
CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH <graph shop>
NODE TABLES (
  <table p.d.orders> AS orders
    KEY(id)
    <options One row per order>
    PROPERTIES(
      id AS order_id,
      amount_usd AS amount <field options Total>,
      customer_id,
      <derived>,
      <measure revenue>
    ),
  <table p.d.customers> AS customers
    KEY(CAST(id AS STRING))
    PROPERTIES(
      CAST(id AS STRING) AS customer_id
    )
)
EDGE TABLES (
  <table p.d.orders> AS placed_by
    KEY(id)
    SOURCE KEY(id) REFERENCES orders(id)
    DESTINATION KEY(customer_id) REFERENCES customers(CAST(id AS STRING))
    <options Who placed it>,
  <table p.d.gifts> AS gifted_to
    KEY(gift_id)
    SOURCE KEY(order_id) REFERENCES orders(id)
    DESTINATION KEY(customer_id) REFERENCES customers(CAST(id AS STRING))
    <options Who received it>
    PROPERTIES(
      card_text AS message <field options Card text>
    ),
  <table ghost> AS from_ghost
    KEY(customer_id)
    SOURCE KEY(customer_id) REFERENCES ghost(customer_id)
    DESTINATION KEY(customer_id) REFERENCES customers(CAST(id AS STRING))
);
`);
       });

  // A subtype of a concrete entity shares its label. The supertype's label
  // loses its OPTIONS, the subtype's remapped `customer_id` gives way to the
  // supertype's, and the subtype's `LABEL orders` block repeats the
  // supertype's properties with the engine's SQL and field metadata. Both
  // warnings name the engine.
  test('a class hierarchy takes its metadata and SQL text from the engine',
       () => {
         const model: SemanticModel = {
           name: 'shop',
           entities: [
             {
               name: 'orders',
               dataSource: 'p.d.orders',
               keys: ['order_id'],
               description: 'One row per order',
               fields: [
                 {name: 'order_id', expression: 'orders.order_id'},
                 {
                   name: 'amount',
                   expression: 'orders.amount',
                   description: 'Total'
                 },
                 {name: 'customer_id', expression: 'orders.customer_id'},
               ],
             },
             {
               name: 'gift_orders',
               dataSource: 'p.d.gift_orders',
               keys: ['order_id'],
               extends: ['orders'],
               description: 'Orders sent as gifts',
               fields: [
                 {name: 'customer_id', expression: 'gift_orders.buyer_id'},
               ],
             },
           ],
           relationships: [],
           metrics: [],
         };
         const {ddl, warnings} =
             generateGraphDdl(model, {...MARKED, placeMetrics: () => new Map()});
         expect(ddl).toBe(`\
CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH <graph shop>
NODE TABLES (
  <table p.d.orders> AS orders
    KEY(id)
    DEFAULT LABEL
    PROPERTIES(
      id AS order_id,
      amount_usd AS amount <field options Total>,
      customer_id
    ),
  <table p.d.gift_orders> AS gift_orders
    KEY(id)
    DEFAULT LABEL
    <options Orders sent as gifts>
    PROPERTIES(
      customer_id,
      id AS order_id,
      amount_usd AS amount <field options Total>
    )
    LABEL orders
    PROPERTIES(
      id AS order_id,
      amount_usd AS amount <field options Total>,
      customer_id
    )
);
`);
         expect(warnings).toEqual([
           `entity 'orders' is a supertype in a class hierarchy; its ` +
               `description/synonyms are dropped from the shared 'orders' ` +
               `label (Marked forbids OPTIONS on a label bound by multiple ` +
               `tables)`,
           `entity 'gift_orders' remaps inherited property 'customer_id' to ` +
               `a different column/expression than its supertype; Marked ` +
               `allows only one definition per property under a shared ` +
               `label, so the supertype's is used and the subclass's ` +
               `remapping is dropped`,
         ]);
       });

  test('warnings name the engine', () => {
    const {warnings} = generateGraphDdl(MODEL, MARKED);
    expect(warnings).toContain(
        `entity 'customers': field 'customer_id' is bound to a non-column ` +
        `expression (CAST(id AS STRING)); a KEY/REFERENCES site ` +
        `requires a bare column, so Marked will reject the generated DDL`);
    expect(warnings).toContain(
        `1 action(s) reach Knowledge Catalog only; the Marked push deploys ` +
        `none of them.`);
    expect(warnings).toContain(
        `1 constraint(s) reach Knowledge Catalog only; the Marked push ` +
        `deploys none of them.`);
    // A field the engine has no SQL for is left out of its node table. One
    // bound by SQL the engine does not read is named against the engine's
    // dialect; one with no SQL at all is unbound.
    expect(warnings).toContain(
        `entity 'orders': field 'notes' has no 'POSTGRES' or 'ANSI_SQL' ` +
        `expression; omitted from the node table`);
    expect(warnings).toContain(
        `entity 'orders': field 'memo' has no column under this binding; ` +
        `omitted from the node table (bind it, or govern the logical model in ` +
        `Knowledge Catalog instead)`);
  });

  test('placeMetrics sees the graph as the shared code built it', () => {
    let seen: {skipped: string[]; ancestorsUsed: string[]; entities: string[]}|
        undefined;
    const model: SemanticModel = {
      ...MODEL,
      entities: [
        ...MODEL.entities,
        {name: 'party', dataSource: '', keys: [], abstract: true, fields: []},
        {
          name: 'keyless',
          dataSource: 'p.d.keyless',
          keys: [],
          fields: [{name: 'x', expression: 'keyless.x'}],
        },
        {
          name: 'vip',
          dataSource: 'p.d.vip',
          keys: ['customer_id'],
          extends: ['party'],
          fields: [{name: 'customer_id', expression: 'vip.customer_id'}],
        },
      ],
    };
    generateGraphDdl(model, {
      ...MARKED,
      placeMetrics: (_metrics, input) => {
        seen = {
          skipped: [...input.skipped].sort(),
          ancestorsUsed: [...input.ancestorsUsed].sort(),
          entities: [...input.entityByName.keys()].sort(),
        };
        return new Map();
      },
    });
    expect(seen).toEqual({
      skipped: ['keyless', 'party'],
      ancestorsUsed: ['party'],
      entities: ['customers', 'keyless', 'orders', 'party', 'vip'],
    });
  });
});

// Unit tests for the Semantic Model IR types and helpers (ir.ts).

import {describe, expect, test} from 'bun:test';

import {
  DialectExpression,
  expressionForDialect,
  Field,
  isFieldBound,
  Metric,
  normalizeDataType,
} from '../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';

describe('expressionForDialect', () => {
  test('returns the exact engine match even when ANSI_SQL appears first', () => {
    const dialects: DialectExpression[] = [
      {dialect: 'ANSI_SQL', expression: 'a + b'},
      {dialect: 'BIGQUERY', expression: 'SAFE_ADD(a, b)'},
    ];
    expect(expressionForDialect({dialects}, 'BIGQUERY')).toBe('SAFE_ADD(a, b)');
  });

  test('falls back to ANSI_SQL when target engine has no entry', () => {
    const dialects: DialectExpression[] = [
      {dialect: 'ANSI_SQL', expression: 'a + b'},
      {dialect: 'BIGQUERY', expression: 'SAFE_ADD(a, b)'},
    ];
    expect(expressionForDialect({dialects}, 'SPANNER')).toBe('a + b');
  });

  test('returns ANSI_SQL directly when targetDialect is ANSI_SQL', () => {
    const dialects: DialectExpression[] = [
      {dialect: 'BIGQUERY', expression: 'SAFE_ADD(a, b)'},
      {dialect: 'ANSI_SQL', expression: 'a + b'},
    ];
    expect(expressionForDialect({dialects}, 'ANSI_SQL')).toBe('a + b');
  });

  test('returns undefined when neither targetDialect nor ANSI_SQL is present', () => {
    const item: Field = {
      name: 'total',
      expression: 'should_not_be_used_when_dialects_is_non_empty',
      dialects: [
        {dialect: 'POSTGRES', expression: 'a + b'},
        {dialect: 'SNOWFLAKE', expression: 'NVL(a, 0) + b'},
      ],
    };
    expect(expressionForDialect(item, 'BIGQUERY')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(expressionForDialect(item, 'SPANNER')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(expressionForDialect(item, 'ANSI_SQL')).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('takes the imported text for its own engine when dialects is absent', () => {
    const item: Field = {
      name: 'total', expression: 'a + b',
      importedExpression: 'NVL(a, 0) + b', importedDialect: 'SNOWFLAKE',
    };
    expect(expressionForDialect(item, 'SNOWFLAKE')).toBe('NVL(a, 0) + b');
    expect(expressionForDialect(item, 'BIGQUERY')).toBe('a + b');
  });

  test('falls back to item.expression when dialects is absent or empty', () => {
    const withoutDialects: Field = {
      name: 'net_amount',
      expression: 'orders.net_amount',
      stringForm: true,
    };
    const withEmptyDialects: Metric = {
      name: 'revenue',
      expression: 'SUM(orders.net_amount)',
      dialects: [],
      stringForm: true,
    };
    const unbound: Field = {
      name: 'unbound_field',
    };

    expect(expressionForDialect(withoutDialects, 'BIGQUERY'))
        .toBe('orders.net_amount');
    expect(expressionForDialect(withoutDialects, 'SPANNER'))
        .toBe('orders.net_amount');
    expect(expressionForDialect(withoutDialects, 'ANSI_SQL'))
        .toBe('orders.net_amount');

    expect(expressionForDialect(withEmptyDialects, 'BIGQUERY'))
        .toBe('SUM(orders.net_amount)');
    expect(expressionForDialect(withEmptyDialects, 'SPANNER'))
        .toBe('SUM(orders.net_amount)');

    expect(expressionForDialect(unbound, 'BIGQUERY')).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe('isFieldBound', () => {
  const bound = (field: Field) => isFieldBound(field);

  test('a non-empty dialect list with no expression is a binding', () => {
    const field: Field = {
      name: 'order_month',
      dialects: [{dialect: 'SNOWFLAKE', expression: "DATE_TRUNC('month', ts)"}],
    };
    expect(bound(field)).toBe(true);
  });

  test('an expression or an imported vendor expression is a binding', () => {
    expect(bound({name: 'a', expression: 'a'})).toBe(true);
    expect(bound({
      name: 'a',
      importedExpression: 'DIV0(a, b)',
      importedDialect: 'SNOWFLAKE',
    })).toBe(true);
  });

  test('an empty dialect list, stringForm or importedDialect alone is not', () => {
    expect(bound({name: 'a'})).toBe(false);
    expect(bound({name: 'a', dialects: []})).toBe(false);
    expect(bound({name: 'a', stringForm: true})).toBe(false);
    expect(bound({name: 'a', importedDialect: 'SNOWFLAKE'})).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('normalizeDataType', () => {
  const CANONICAL = [
    'String',
    'Integer',
    'Decimal',
    'Float',
    'Boolean',
    'Date',
    'Time',
    'DateTime',
    'DateTimeTz',
  ] as const;

  test('0.2.0.dev0 accepts all nine exact-case canonical names', () => {
    for (const name of CANONICAL) {
      expect(normalizeDataType(name, '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({
        ok: true,
        type: name,
      });
    }
  });

  test('0.2.0.dev0 rejects non-canonical casing and unknown types', () => {
    expect(normalizeDataType('integer', '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({ok: false});
    expect(normalizeDataType('STRING', '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({ok: false});
    expect(normalizeDataType('opaque', '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({ok: false});
    expect(normalizeDataType('VARCHAR', '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({ok: false});
  });

  test('0.2.0.dev0 normalizes Opaque and undefined to type: undefined', () => {
    expect(normalizeDataType('Opaque', '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType(undefined, '0.2.0.dev0')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
  });

  test('0.2.0.dev0/google accepts any casing and returns the canonical spelling', () => {
    for (const name of CANONICAL) {
      expect(normalizeDataType(name, '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
        ok: true,
        type: name,
      });
      expect(normalizeDataType(name.toLowerCase(), '0.2.0.dev0/google'))
          .toEqual({
            ok: true,
            type: name,
          });
      expect(normalizeDataType(name.toUpperCase(), '0.2.0.dev0/google'))
          .toEqual({
            ok: true,
            type: name,
          });
    }
    expect(normalizeDataType('datetime', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: 'DateTime',
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType('datetimetz', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: 'DateTimeTz',
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType('DATETIMETZ', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: 'DateTimeTz',
    });
  });

  test('0.2.0.dev0/google normalizes Opaque in any casing and undefined to type: undefined', () => {
    expect(normalizeDataType('Opaque', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType('opaque', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType('OPAQUE', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType(undefined, '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      type: undefined,
    });
  });

  test('0.2.0.dev0/google rejects unknown physical types', () => {
    expect(normalizeDataType('VARCHAR', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: false,
    });
    expect(normalizeDataType('INT64', '0.2.0.dev0/google')).toEqual({
      ok: false,
    });
  });
});
