# A COMBINED single-file model: the logical declarations AND an inline physical
# binding (the implicit `default` profile) in one file -- the form a model has
# before any profile exists. Every field is bound to a column here, so this file
# deploys on its own with a bare `kcmd push`. A profile merges over these
# inline bindings: a field it binds takes the profile's column, a field it
# excludes is unbound, and every other field keeps the binding here. The
# profiles beside it re-declare the columns each store serves:
#   - prod:  an environment swap -- the same columns, a different project/dataset.
#   - remap: a store that renamed a column and does not carry `discount`.
version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: sales
    deployment_target: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme-dev/datasets/sales/propertyGraphs/sales
    entities:
      - name: Customer
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme-dev/datasets/sales/tables/customers
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - { name: id, label: Customer ID, expression: customer_id }
          - { name: name, expression: customer_name }
      - name: Order
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/acme-dev/datasets/sales/tables/orders
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - { name: id, expression: order_id }
          - { name: customerId, expression: customer_id }
          - { name: amount, expression: amount }
          - { name: discount, expression: discount }

// Behavior specification for deriving action tools and schema metadata from a
// model.

import {describe, expect, test} from 'bun:test';
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';

import {Action, Constraint, Entity, SemanticModel} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';
import {loadModels} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/loader';
import {resolveInheritance} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/resolve_inheritance';
import {actionTools, modelTools, readableEntities} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/agent_tools';
import {dialectFor} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/dialect';
import {SemanticRuntime} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/runtime';

const FIXTURES = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'fixtures');

function rt(
    model: SemanticModel,
    over: Partial<SemanticRuntime> = {}): SemanticRuntime {
  return {
    model,
    document: 'test',
    store: {
      kind: 'spanner',
      name: 'projects/p/instances/i/databases/d',
      project: 'p',
      instance: 'i',
      database: 'd',
    },
    profile: 'default',
    entryGroup: 'eg',
    ...over,
  };
}

function loadFixtureModel(name: string): SemanticModel {
  return loadModels(
             fs.readFileSync(path.join(FIXTURES, name), 'utf8'),
             {allowLegacyBareSource: true})
      .models[0];
}

function withExecutor(
    model: SemanticModel, over: Partial<Action>): SemanticModel {
  const [action] = model.actions!;
  return {...model, actions: [{...action, ...over}]};
}

const RUNNABLE: Partial<Action> = {
  executor: {
    kind: 'sql',
    sql: {statements: ['UPDATE orders SET o_totalprice = 0 WHERE 1 = 0']},
  },
  guards: [],
};


describe('action tools', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');
  const tools = actionTools({runtime: rt(model)});

  test('one tool per action, named the way tool APIs expect', () => {
    expect(tools).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(tools[0].name).toBe('place_order');
    expect(tools[0].actionName).toBe('PlaceOrder');
  });

  test(
      'every parameter asks for a scalar, whichever way it was written', () => {
        const byName =
            Object.fromEntries(tools[0].parameters.map(p => [p.name, p]));

        expect(byName['customer'].type).toBe('integer');
        expect(byName['customer'].description)
            .toBe('The customer\'s account number.');

        expect(byName['quantity'].type).toBe('integer');
        expect(byName['quantity'].description).toContain('whole number');
      });

  test('every action parameter is required by default', () => {
    expect(tools[0].parameters.every(p => p.required)).toBe(true);
    expect(tools[0].parameters.map(p => p.name))
        .toEqual(model.actions![0].parameters.map(p => p.name));
  });

  test('a model with no actions yields no write tools', () => {
    const readOnly: SemanticModel = {...model, actions: []};
    expect(actionTools({runtime: rt(readOnly)})).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('a tool offers no way to approve anything', () => {
    const names = tools[0].parameters.map(p => p.name.toLowerCase());
    expect(names.some(n => n.includes('approv'))).toBe(false);
    expect(Object.keys(tools[0])).not.toContain('approvals');
  });

  test(
      'authored parameter descriptions and optional/default flags reach the tool',
      () => {
        const custom = withExecutor(model, {
          parameters: [
            {
              name: 'source',
              type: 'Integer',
              concept: 'customer',
              field: 'id',
              description: 'The account money leaves.',
            },
            {
              name: 'currency',
              type: 'String',
              description: 'ISO currency code.',
              default: 'USD',
            },
            {
              name: 'memo',
              type: 'String',
              required: false,
            },
          ],
        });
        const [tool] = actionTools({runtime: rt(custom)});
        const byName =
            Object.fromEntries(tool.parameters.map(p => [p.name, p]));

        expect(byName['source'].description).toBe('The account money leaves.');
        expect(byName['source'].type).toBe('integer');
        expect(byName['source'].required).toBe(true);

        expect(byName['currency'].description).toBe('ISO currency code.');
        expect(byName['currency'].required).toBe(false);
        expect(byName['currency'].default).toBe('USD');

        expect(byName['memo'].required).toBe(false);
      });
});


describe('what counts as runnable under a profile', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  function guardedBy(constraint: Constraint, guard: string): SemanticModel {
    const base = withExecutor(model, {...RUNNABLE, guards: [guard]});
    return {...base, constraints: [constraint]};
  }

  test('an action runnable here is marked so, with no excuse attached', () => {
    const [tool] = actionTools({runtime: rt(withExecutor(model, RUNNABLE))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('a remote executor (MCP, REST, gRPC) is runnable even without a store',
       () => {
         const [tool] =
             actionTools({runtime: rt(model, {store: undefined})});
         expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
         expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
       });

  test('a sql executor with no store at all is not runnable', () => {
    const [tool] = actionTools(
        {runtime: rt(withExecutor(model, RUNNABLE), {store: undefined})});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(false);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toContain('no store');
  });

  // BigQuery executes DML like the other two backends, so binding one is not a
  // reason to withhold an action. A warehouse write costs what a warehouse
  // write costs, but that is the author's call to make, not a rule enforced
  // here -- and the push-time pre-flight plans these statements against
  // BigQuery too, which would be incoherent if they could never run.
  test('a sql executor bound to BigQuery is runnable', () => {
    const [tool] = actionTools({
      runtime: rt(withExecutor(model, RUNNABLE), {
        store: {
          kind: 'bigquery',
          name: 'projects/p/datasets/sales_ds',
          project: 'p',
          dataset: 'sales_ds',
        },
      }),
    });
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('an action with no executor blames the binding, not the action', () => {
    const unbound = withExecutor(model, {executor: undefined, guards: []});
    const [tool] = actionTools({runtime: rt(unbound)});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(false);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toContain('no executor');
    expect(tool.unavailable).toContain('somewhere else');
  });

  test('a guard that only warns does not withhold the tool', () => {
    const advisory: Constraint = {
      name: 'AmountIsLarge',
      judgment: 'A quantity over 1000 should be called out.',
      onViolation: 'warn',
    };
    const [tool] =
        actionTools({runtime: rt(guardedBy(advisory, 'AmountIsLarge'))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('a well-formed judged guard is runnable', () => {
    const judged: Constraint = {
      name: 'CreditIsJustified',
      judgment: 'The memo must name what went wrong.',
      onViolation: 'reject',
    };
    const [tool] =
        actionTools({runtime: rt(guardedBy(judged, 'CreditIsJustified'))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('a guard naming nothing the model declares withholds the tool', () => {
    const other: Constraint = {
      name: 'SomethingElse',
      judgment: 'Something else must hold.',
      onViolation: 'reject',
    };
    const [tool] = actionTools({runtime: rt(guardedBy(other, 'NoSuchRule'))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(false);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toContain('NoSuchRule');
  });

  test('a guard whose constraint states no rule text withholds the tool', () => {
    const bodyless: Constraint = {
      name: 'QuantityIsPositive',
      onViolation: 'reject',
    };
    const [tool] =
        actionTools({runtime: rt(guardedBy(bodyless, 'QuantityIsPositive'))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(false);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toContain('states no rule to put to a judge');
  });
});


describe('the shape of an entity key withholds no tool', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  test('a key in two parts is offered like any other', () => {
    const composite = {
      ...model,
      entities: model.entities.map(
          e => e.name === 'customer' ?
              {...e, keys: ['c_custkey', 'c_nationkey']} :
              e),
    };
    const [tool] =
        actionTools({runtime: rt(withExecutor(composite, RUNNABLE))});
    expect(tool.runnable).toBe(true);
    expect(tool.unavailable).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('a caller names each part of it as an ordinary parameter', () => {
    const twoPart = withExecutor(model, {
      ...RUNNABLE,
      parameters: [
        {
          name: 'custkey',
          type: 'Integer',
          concept: 'customer',
          field: 'c_custkey'
        },
        {
          name: 'nationkey',
          type: 'Integer',
          concept: 'customer',
          field: 'c_nationkey'
        },
      ],
    });
    const [tool] = actionTools({runtime: rt(twoPart)});
    expect(tool.parameters.map(p => [p.name, p.type])).toEqual([
      ['custkey', 'integer'],
      ['nationkey', 'integer'],
    ]);
  });
});


describe('parameter formatting', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  test(
      'authored parameter descriptions normalize terminators and keep temporal format guidance',
      () => {
        const base = withExecutor(model, {
          ...RUNNABLE,
          parameters: [
            {
              name: 'customer',
              type: 'Integer',
              concept: 'customer',
              field: 'id',
              description: 'The buyer'
            },
            {

            },

            .toBe('When the transfer settles. As a date, YYYY-MM-DD.');
      });

describe('one name space for everything a model offers', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  test('two actions that snake-case alike are still told apart', () => {
    const twins = {
      ...model,
      actions: [
        {...model.actions![0], name: 'IssueCredit'},
        {...model.actions![0], name: 'issue-credit'},
      ],
    };
    const {actions} = modelTools({runtime: rt(twins)});
    expect(actions.map(t => t.name)).toEqual([
      'issue_credit', 'issue_credit_2'
    ]);
  });

  test('nothing is renamed when nothing collides', () => {
    const {actions} = modelTools({runtime: rt(model)});
    expect(actions.map(t => t.name)).toEqual(['place_order']);
  });

describe('the instruction an agent is given comes from the model', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  test('the model\'s own words come first, verbatim', () => {
    const stated = {
      ...model,
      aiContext: {instructions: 'You work a returns desk for this business.'},
    };
    const {instruction} = modelTools({runtime: rt(stated)});
    expect(instruction.startsWith('You work a returns desk for this business.'))
        .toBe(true);
  });

  test(

        const {instruction} = modelTools({runtime: rt(model)});
        expect(model.aiContext?.instructions).toBeUndefined();

      });

  test('the two parts are separated, not run together', () => {
    const stated = {
      ...model,
      aiContext: {instructions: 'You work a returns desk.'},
    };
    const {instruction} = modelTools({runtime: rt(stated)});
    expect(instruction).toContain('You work a returns desk.\n\nNever invent');
  });
});


describe('an entity whose fields await transpilation', () => {
  const model = loadFixtureModel('actions_place_order.yaml');

  function untranspiled(name: string): Entity[] {
    return model.entities.map(entity => {
      if (entity.name !== name) return entity;
      return {
        ...entity,
        fields: entity.fields.map(field => ({
                                    ...field,
                                    expression: undefined,
                                    importedExpression: field.expression,
                                    importedDialect: 'SNOWFLAKE',
                                  })),
      };
    });
  }

  test('yields the same readable schema it would after transpilation', () => {
    const baseRuntime = rt(model);
    const dialect = dialectFor(baseRuntime.store);
    const before = readableEntities(baseRuntime, dialect)
                       .find(r => r.entity.name === 'customer')!;
    const after =
        readableEntities(
            rt({...model, entities: untranspiled('customer')}), dialect)
            .find(r => r.entity.name === 'customer')!;
    expect(after.fields).toEqual(before.fields);
  });
});


describe('a column binding with a comment', () => {
  const model: SemanticModel = {
    name: 'm',
    relationships: [],
    metrics: [],
    entities: [{
      name: 'orders',
      dataSource: 'orders',
      keys: ['id'],
      fields: [
        {name: 'id', expression: 'order_id -- the key'},
        {name: 'amount', expression: '/* in cents */ amount'},
        {name: 'status', expression: 'status # open or closed'},
      ],
    }],
  };
  const columns = (runtime: SemanticRuntime) =>
      readableEntities(runtime, dialectFor(runtime.store))
          .flatMap(r => r.fields.map(f => f.column));

  test('still names its column', () => {
    expect(columns(rt(model))).toEqual(['order_id', 'amount', 'status']);
  });

  test('is read in the store\'s SQL, on every entity that has it', () => {
    // GoogleSQL reads `#` as a comment and PostgreSQL reads it as an operator,
    // so on an AlloyDB store `status # open or closed` names no single column.
    // An imported text is read in its own dialect, so the PostgreSQL
    // `flags # 1` names no single column on any store. The runtime resolves
    // inheritance in the store's SQL too.
    const {models} = loadModels(`version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: m
    entities:
      - name: person
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/d/tables/person
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - {name: id, expression: id}
          - {name: status, expression: "status # open or closed"}
          - name: flags
            expression:
              dialects: [{dialect: POSTGRES, expression: "flags # 1"}]
      - name: customer
        extends: [person]
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/d/tables/customer
        primary_key: [id]
`);
    const byEntity = (runtime: SemanticRuntime) => Object.fromEntries(
        readableEntities(runtime, dialectFor(runtime.store))
            .map(r => [r.entity.name, r.fields.map(f => f.column)]));
    expect(byEntity(rt(resolveInheritance(models[0]).model)))
        .toEqual({person: ['id', 'status'], customer: ['id', 'status']});
    const alloyDb = rt(resolveInheritance(models[0], 'POSTGRES').model, {
      store: {
        kind: 'alloydb',
        name: 'projects/p/locations/l/clusters/c/databases/d',
        project: 'p',
        location: 'l',
        cluster: 'c',
        instance: 'i',
        database: 'd',
      },
    });
    expect(byEntity(alloyDb)).toEqual({person: ['id'], customer: ['id']});
  });

  test('is read as the graph generators read it, even when a vendor entry holds the same text', () => {
    // PostgreSQL reads `#` as an operator, and the bundled parser does not read
    // it as a comment in MySQL. The BIGQUERY and ANSI_SQL texts are read as
    // BigQuery reads them, where `#` starts a comment.
    const {models} = loadModels(`version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"
semantic_model:
  - name: m
    entities:
      - name: person
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/d/tables/person
        primary_key: [id]
        fields:
          - {name: id, expression: id}
          - name: amount
            expression:
              dialects:
                - {dialect: POSTGRES, expression: "amount # in cents"}
                - {dialect: BIGQUERY, expression: "amount # in cents"}
          - name: status
            expression:
              dialects:
                - {dialect: MYSQL, expression: "status # open or closed"}
                - {dialect: ANSI_SQL, expression: "status # open or closed"}
      - name: customer
        extends: [person]
        source: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/d/tables/customer
        primary_key: [id]
`);
    const runtime = rt(resolveInheritance(models[0]).model);
    const byEntity = Object.fromEntries(
        readableEntities(runtime, dialectFor(runtime.store))
            .map(r => [r.entity.name, r.fields.map(f => f.column)]));
    expect(byEntity).toEqual({
      person: ['id', 'amount', 'status'],
      customer: ['id', 'amount', 'status'],
    });
  });
});

FILE: toolbox/mdcode/tests/libts/semantic/runtime/store.test.ts

// Behavior specification for resolving a model's store.
//
// The claim under test is that a model says where it lives and nothing else
// does. A caller -- the CLI, an agent, a setup script -- asks the model and
// gets one answer, and a model whose bindings disagree with its deployment
// target gets a refusal rather than a write into whichever database happened
// to be named last.
//
// Nothing here opens a connection. Deciding where to write is pure, and the
// AlloyDB instance listing is mocked.

import {describe, expect, spyOn, test} from 'bun:test';

import {AlloyDbClient, Instance} from '../../../../src/libts/gcp/alloydb';
import * as api from '../../../../src/libts/gcp/api';
import {ApiContext} from '../../../../src/libts/gcp/context';
import {SemanticModel} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';
import {loadModels} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/loader';
import {AlloyDbDatabase, resolveStore, storeLine, withPrimaryInstance} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/store';

const DB = '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instances/i/databases/d';
const DATASET = '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/s';
const PG =
    '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/instances/i/databases/d';

function model(body: string): SemanticModel {
  const loaded = loadModels(
      `version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"\nsemantic_model:\n  - name: m\n${body}`,
      {bindingOptional: true, allowLegacyBareSource: true});
  return loaded.models[0];
}

function bound(target: string, source: string): SemanticModel {
  return model(
      `    deployment_target: ${target}\n` +
      `    entities:\n` +
      `      - name: Customer\n` +
      `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
      `        source: ${source}\n` +
      `        fields:\n` +
      `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
}


describe('where a model says it lives', () => {
  test('the deployment target is the store, split into its parts', () => {
    const store =
        resolveStore(bound(`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DB}/tables/Customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('spanner');
    if (store.kind !== 'spanner') return;
    expect(store.project).toBe('p');
    expect(store.instance).toBe('i');
    expect(store.database).toBe('d');
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
  });

  // A resource name is the URI without the leading `//`, so a model written
  // either way, or mixing the two, runs against the same store, and its table
  // is in that store rather than reported as bound elsewhere.
  test('a target and a source written as resource names give the same store', () => {
    const name = DB.slice(2);
    for (const [target, source] of [
           [`${name}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${name}/tables/Customer`],
           [`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${name}/tables/Customer`],
           [`${name}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DB}/tables/Customer`],
         ]) {
      const store = resolveStore(bound(target, source));
      if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
      expect(store.kind).toBe('spanner');
      expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
    }
  });

  test('a BigQuery target is a store like any other', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        bound(`${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DATASET}/tables/Customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('bigquery');
    if (store.kind !== 'bigquery') return;
    expect(store.project).toBe('p');
    expect(store.dataset).toBe('s');
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/datasets/s');
  });

  test('an AlloyDB target is a store, down to the database', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(bound(PG, `${PG}/tables/customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
    if (store.kind !== 'alloydb') return;
    expect(store.project).toBe('p');
    expect(store.location).toBe('us-central1');
    expect(store.cluster).toBe('c');
    expect(store.instance).toBe('i');
    expect(store.database).toBe('d');
    // The instance-based URI names the same database as the cluster-based
    // one, so the store takes the same name.
    expect(store.name).toBe(
        'projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d');
  });

  // The instance-based URI names the instance to connect through, so it is
  // kept in either order.
  test('one AlloyDB database named by both of its URIs is one store', () => {
    const byInstance = `      - {name: by_instance, target: "${PG}"}\n`;
    const byCluster =
        `      - {name: by_cluster, target: "//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d"}\n`;
    for (const listed of [byInstance + byCluster, byCluster + byInstance]) {
      const store = resolveStore(model(
          `    deployments:\n` + listed +
          `    entities:\n` +
          `      - name: Customer\n` +
          `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
          `        source: ${PG}/tables/customer\n` +
          `        fields:\n` +
          `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`));
      if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
      expect(store.kind === 'alloydb' && store.instance).toBe('i');
    }
  });

  // Two profiles that name one AlloyDB database describe one store, whichever
  // URI each uses.
  test('one AlloyDB database has one store name in every profile', () => {
    const m = model(
        `    deployments:\n` +
        `      - {name: old, target: "${PG}", profile: legacy}\n` +
        `      - {name: new, target: "//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d"}\n` +
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        source: ${PG}/tables/customer\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
    const byInstance = resolveStore(m, 'legacy');
    const byCluster = resolveStore(m, 'default');
    if ('error' in byInstance) throw new Error(byInstance.error);
    if ('error' in byCluster) throw new Error(byCluster.error);
    expect(byInstance.name)
        .toBe('projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d');
    expect(byCluster.name).toBe(byInstance.name);
  });

  // An AlloyDB target names a DATABASE, not a graph, because AlloyDB has no
  // property-graph DDL to address. A URI carrying the graph segment the other
  // two backends use names nothing that could be created, so it is not quietly
  // accepted.
  test('an AlloyDB target with a graph segment is not a target at all', () => {
    const store =
        resolveStore(bound(`${PG}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${PG}/tables/customer`));
    expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
    if (!('error' in store)) return;
    expect(store.error).toContain(
        'which is not a BigQuery graph, a Spanner graph or an AlloyDB database');
    expect(store.error).toContain('propertyGraphs/g');
  });

  test('a model with no deployment target has no store', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(model(
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`));
    expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
    if (!('error' in store)) return;
    expect(store.error).toContain('no deployment target');
  });
});


describe('a binding that disagrees with the target', () => {
  // An action's statements name a table and drop the qualifier, so a write
  // against a stray binding still runs -- against whatever table of that name
  // the TARGET store holds. Nothing downstream would report it, which is why
  // it is refused here.
  test('an entity bound to another database is refused, and both are named',
       () => {
         const other =
             '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instances/i/databases/other';
         const store = resolveStore(
             bound(`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${other}/tables/Customer`));
         expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
         if (!('error' in store)) return;
         expect(store.error).toContain('databases/other');
         expect(store.error).toContain('deployment target is projects/p');
       });

  test('an entity bound to another system is refused for the same reason',
       () => {
         const store = resolveStore(bound(
             `${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DATASET}/tables/Customer`));
         expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
         if (!('error' in store)) return;
         expect(store.error).toContain("'Customer' to p.s.Customer");
         expect(store.error)
             .toContain('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
       });

  test('an entity this profile binds to nothing is not a mis-binding', () => {
    // Declared and unbound is a model that has not been given a table yet.
    // The statements report that themselves, naming the table they could not
    // find; refusing here would refuse a logical model for being logical.
    const store = resolveStore(model(
        `    deployment_target: ${DB}/propertyGraphs/g\n` +
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer}\n`));
    expect('error' in store).toBe(false);
  });

  // A BigQuery graph may read tables in another dataset, and push accepts
  // that, so the store gives none and does not fail.
  test('a BigQuery table in another dataset gives no store and does not fail it',
       () => {
         const store = resolveStore(bound(
             `${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`,
             '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/raw/tables/customer'));
         expect(store).toEqual({
           error: expect.stringContaining("binds 'Customer' to p.raw.customer"),
         });
       });
});


// A model may name more than one destination: the same graph published to
// BigQuery for analysis and to Spanner for operations is one model deployed
// twice, not two models. Which of those is the store an action runs against is
// not in doubt -- only Spanner accepts a write -- so the pair resolves. Two
// destinations of the SAME backend is the case nothing here can decide.
describe('a model that declares more than one deployment target', () => {
  // A vanilla model, whose targets sit in a GOOGLE block.
  function targets(uris: string[], source: string): SemanticModel {
    return {
      ...bound(`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, source),
      version: '0.2.0.dev0',
      deployments: undefined,
      customExtensions: [{
        vendorName: 'GOOGLE',
        data: JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: uris}),
      }],
    };
  }

  test('Spanner alongside BigQuery resolves to the Spanner store', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(targets(
        [`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`],
        `${DB}/tables/Customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('spanner');
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
  });

  test('two Spanner targets is ambiguous, and the message says which backend',
       () => {
         const store = resolveStore(targets(
             [`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instances/i/databases/d2/propertyGraphs/g`],
             `${DB}/tables/Customer`));
         expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
         if (!('error' in store)) return;
         expect(store.error).toContain('2 Spanner deployment targets');
         expect(store.error)
             .toContain("in its GOOGLE block's 'deploymentTargets'");
         expect(store.error).toContain('the runtime uses exactly one deployment for now.');
       });

  // Ambiguity is about ROLE, not about backend. Spanner alongside AlloyDB is
  // two targets that could each serve the same one -- both hold the rows, both
  // take the write -- so it is as undecidable as two of either, and the message
  // has to name both rather than reporting "2 Spanner" or picking a winner.
  test('Spanner alongside AlloyDB is ambiguous, and both are named', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        targets([`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, PG], `${DB}/tables/Customer`));
    expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
    if (!('error' in store)) return;
    expect(store.error).toContain('1 Spanner and 1 AlloyDB');
    expect(store.error).toContain('two operational backends');
    expect(store.error)
        .toContain("in its GOOGLE block's 'deploymentTargets'");
    expect(store.error).toContain('the runtime uses exactly one deployment for now.');
  });

  test('AlloyDB alongside BigQuery resolves to the AlloyDB store', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        targets([PG, `${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`], `${PG}/tables/customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
  });

  test('two BigQuery targets is ambiguous in the same way', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(targets(
        [`${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`, `//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/s2/propertyGraphs/g`],
        `${DATASET}/tables/Customer`));
    expect('error' in store).toBe(true);
    if (!('error' in store)) return;
    expect(store.error).toContain('2 BigQuery deployment targets');
  });

  // Only the two URIs of one AlloyDB database are merged. A target listed
  // twice in a GOOGLE block is a duplicate, which every push refuses.
  test('one Spanner graph listed twice is a duplicate target', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(targets(
        [`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`],
        `${DB}/tables/Customer`));
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain(`declares duplicate deployment target '${DB}/propertyGraphs/g'`);
  });

  test('one AlloyDB URI listed twice is a duplicate target', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(targets([PG, PG], `${PG}/tables/customer`));
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain(`declares duplicate deployment target '${PG}'`);
  });

  test('two instances of one AlloyDB database are ambiguous', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(targets(
        [PG, PG.replace('/instances/i/', '/instances/i2/')],
        `${PG}/tables/customer`));
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain('2 AlloyDB deployment targets');
  });

  // A vanilla model whose GOOGLE block lists 'deploymentTargets' is told about
  // that key, and how to list a deployment in the block.
  test('a GOOGLE block with no target names the block', () => {
    expect(resolveStore(targets([], `${DB}/tables/Customer`))).toEqual({
      error: "Model 'm' declares no deployment target in its GOOGLE block's " +
          "'deploymentTargets', so there is no store to run against. In a " +
          "GOOGLE custom_extensions block on the model, declare a " +
          "deployment in 'deployments' whose target names a database.",
    });
  });

  // The loader removes a GOOGLE block that lists no 'deploymentTargets', so a
  // vanilla model with no target and no such block is told about
  // 'deployments'.
  test('a vanilla model with no deploymentTargets block is told about deployments', () => {
    const none = {...targets([], `${DB}/tables/Customer`), customExtensions: undefined};
    expect(resolveStore(none)).toEqual({
      error: "Model 'm' declares no deployment target in 'deployments', so " +
          'there is no store to run against. In a GOOGLE custom_extensions ' +
          "block on the model, declare a deployment in 'deployments' whose " +
          'target names a database.',
    });
  });

  // A GOOGLE block names no deployment, so the message names the block. Push
  // rejects each of these models, so the store fails rather than being none.
  test('a GOOGLE block target in no accepted form is reported, alone or beside one that gives a store',
       () => {
         const typo =
             '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instance/i/databases/d/propertyGraphs/g';
         const notAccepted = {
           error: `Model 'm': the GOOGLE custom_extension's ` +
               `'deploymentTargets' lists '${typo}', which is not a BigQuery ` +
               `graph, a Spanner graph or an AlloyDB database. Write a ` +
               `resource URI: ` +
               `'//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/datasets/<d>/propertyGraphs/<g>', ` +
               `'//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/instances/<i>/databases/<db>/propertyGraphs/<g>' ` +
               `or '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/locations/<l>/clusters/<c>/databases/<db>'.`,
           named: true,
           rejected: true,
         };
         expect(resolveStore(targets(
                    [`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, typo], `${DB}/tables/Customer`)))
             .toEqual(notAccepted);
         expect(resolveStore(targets([typo], `${DB}/tables/Customer`)))
             .toEqual(notAccepted);
         expect(resolveStore(targets(
                    ['spanner:graph:p.regional-us.i.d.g'],
                    `${DB}/tables/Customer`)))
             .toEqual({
               error: `Model 'm': the GOOGLE custom_extension's ` +
                   `'deploymentTargets' lists 'spanner:graph:p.regional-us.i.d.g', ` +
                   `which is a Knowledge Catalog name. Write the resource URI ` +
                   `instead: ` +
                   `'//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/instances/<i>/databases/<db>/propertyGraphs/<g>'.`,
               named: true,
               rejected: true,
             });
       });

  // Push reports the same JSON error.
  test('a GOOGLE block whose data is not valid JSON is reported, not thrown',
       () => {
         const broken: SemanticModel = {
           ...bound(`${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, `${DB}/tables/Customer`),
           deployments: undefined,
           customExtensions: [{vendorName: 'GOOGLE', data: '{not-json'}],
         };
         expect(resolveStore(broken)).toEqual({
           error: "Model 'm': GOOGLE custom_extension 'data' is not valid JSON.",
           named: true,
           rejected: true,
         });
       });
});


// A model names its stores in `deployments:`, each for the profile it names or
// for `default` when it names none. The runtime asks for one profile's store.
describe('the store a profile uses', () => {
  const BQ_GRAPH = `${DATASET}/propertyGraphs/g`;
  const SPANNER_GRAPH = `${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`;
  const CLUSTER_DB =
      '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d';

  function deployed(entries: string, source = ''): SemanticModel {
    return model(
        `    deployments:\n${entries}` +
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        (source ? `        source: ${source}\n` : '') +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
  }

  const threeProfiles = deployed(
      `      - {name: bq_prod, target: "${BQ_GRAPH}", profile: analytical}\n` +
      `      - {name: spanner_prod, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}", profile: operational}\n` +
      `      - {name: alloy_prod, target: "${CLUSTER_DB}"}\n`);

  test('each profile takes the deployment that names it', () => {
    const operational = resolveStore(threeProfiles, 'operational');
    if ('error' in operational) throw new Error(operational.error);
    expect(operational.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
    const analytical = resolveStore(threeProfiles, 'analytical');
    if ('error' in analytical) throw new Error(analytical.error);
    expect(analytical.name).toBe('projects/p/datasets/s');
  });

  test('default takes the deployment that names no profile', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(threeProfiles, 'default');
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
    if (store.kind !== 'alloydb') return;
    // A cluster target names no instance; the runtime finds it.
    expect(store.instance).toBeUndefined();
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d');
  });

  test('a profile no deployment uses has no store', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(threeProfiles, 'staging');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toBe(
            "binding profile 'staging' is a named profile, which names no " +
            "deployment target, and no deployment in 'deployments' uses it, so " +
            'there is no database to run it against');
  });

  test('default has no store when every deployment names a profile', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        deployed(
            `      - {name: bq_prod, target: "${BQ_GRAPH}", profile: analytical}\n`),
        'default');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain(
            "Model 'm' declares no deployment without a 'profile' in " +
            "'deployments'");
  });

  test('of several, the single operational store is taken', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        deployed(
            `      - {name: bq_prod, target: "${BQ_GRAPH}"}\n` +
                `      - {name: spanner_prod, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n`,
            `${DB}/tables/Customer`),
        'default');
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('spanner');
  });

  test('several with no single operational store fail, naming them', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        deployed(
            `      - {name: spanner_a, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}", profile: operational}\n` +
            `      - {name: spanner_b, target: "${DB}2/propertyGraphs/g", profile: operational}\n` +
            `      - {name: spanner_c, target: "${DB}3/propertyGraphs/g"}\n`),
        'operational');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain(
            "declares 2 Spanner deployment targets in 'deployments' for " +
            "profile 'operational' (spanner_a, spanner_b), so which store it " +
            'runs against is ambiguous');
  });

  // A vanilla model whose GOOGLE block holds `data`.
  function vanillaModel(data: object): SemanticModel {
    return loadModels(
        `version: "0.2.0.dev0"\nsemantic_model:\n  - name: m\n` +
        `    custom_extensions:\n` +
        `      - vendor_name: GOOGLE\n` +
        `        data: '${JSON.stringify(data)}'\n` +
        `    datasets:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        source: ${DB}/tables/Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - name: id\n` +
        `            expression: {dialects: [{dialect: SPANNER, expression: id}]}\n`)
        .models[0];
  }

  // A vanilla model lists its deployments in its GOOGLE block, and the
  // messages say so, as push's do.
  test('several block deployments of a vanilla model fail, naming the block', () => {
    const vanilla = vanillaModel({
      deployments: [
        {name: 'spanner_a', target: SPANNER_GRAPH},
        {name: 'spanner_b', target: `${DB}2/propertyGraphs/g`},
      ],
    });
    const store = resolveStore(vanilla, 'default');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain(
            "declares 2 Spanner deployment targets in its GOOGLE block's " +
            "'deployments' for profile 'default' (spanner_a, spanner_b), so " +
            'which store it runs against is ambiguous');
  });

  test('default has no store when every block deployment names a profile, naming the block', () => {
    const vanilla = vanillaModel({
      profiles: [{name: 'operational'}],
      deployments: [{name: 'spanner_a', target: SPANNER_GRAPH, profile: 'operational'}],
    });
    const store = resolveStore(vanilla, 'default');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toBe(
            "Model 'm' declares no deployment without a 'profile' in its " +
            "GOOGLE block's 'deployments', so there is no store to run " +
            "against under binding profile 'default'.");
  });

  test('a block profile no block deployment uses has no store, naming the block', () => {
    const vanilla = vanillaModel({
      profiles: [{name: 'operational'}, {name: 'staging'}],
      deployments: [{name: 'spanner_a', target: SPANNER_GRAPH, profile: 'operational'}],
    });
    const store = resolveStore(vanilla, 'staging');
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toBe(
            "binding profile 'staging' is a named profile, which names no " +
            "deployment target, and no deployment in its GOOGLE block's " +
            "'deployments' uses it, so there is no database to run it against");
  });

  test('a deployment that names no destination is reported beside one that does',
       () => {
         const typo =
             '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instance/i/databases/d/propertyGraphs/g';
         const store = resolveStore(
             deployed(
                 `      - {name: good, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n` +
                     `      - {name: bad, target: "${typo}"}\n`,
                 `${DB}/tables/Customer`),
             'default');
         expect('error' in store && store.error)
             .toContain(
                 `Model 'm': deployment 'bad' targets '${typo}', which is ` +
                 'not a BigQuery graph, a Spanner graph or an AlloyDB database');
       });

  test('a lone deployment in no accepted form is reported the same way', () => {
    const target = 'bigquery:graph:p.s.g';
    const store = resolveStore(
        deployed(`      - {name: prod, target: "${target}"}\n`), 'default');
    expect(store).toEqual({
      error: `Model 'm': deployment 'prod' targets '${target}', which is a ` +
          `Knowledge Catalog name. Write the resource URI instead: ` +
          `'//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/<p>/datasets/<d>/propertyGraphs/<g>'.`,
      named: true,
      rejected: true,
    });
  });

  // Every AlloyDB target pushed before the cluster form holds the
  // instance-based URI, so the runtime still reads it in a list.
  test('an instance-based AlloyDB target in a list is still read', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        deployed(
            `      - {name: alloy_old, target: "${PG}"}\n`,
            '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/' +
                'clusters/c/databases/d/schemas/public/tables/customer'),
        'default');
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind === 'alloydb' && store.instance).toBe('i');
  });

  // A vanilla model keeps its targets in a GOOGLE block, which names no
  // profile, so they are for the model's own bindings.
  test('a GOOGLE block gives no store to a named profile', () => {
    const vanilla: SemanticModel = {
      ...deployed(`      - {name: x, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n`),
      version: '0.2.0.dev0',
      deployments: undefined,
    };
    expect(resolveStore(vanilla, 'prod'))
        .toEqual({
          error: "binding profile 'prod' is a named profile, which names no " +
              'deployment target, so there is no database to run it against',
        });
    const store = resolveStore(vanilla, 'default');
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('spanner');
  });

  // A legacy wrapper merged into a model with no deployments has no target.
  test('a legacy wrapper over a model with no deployments has no store', () => {
    const noTarget: SemanticModel = {
      ...deployed(`      - {name: x, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n`),
      deployments: undefined,
      customExtensions: undefined,
    };
    expect(resolveStore(noTarget, 'prod', {legacyWrapper: true}))
        .toEqual({
          error: "Model 'm' declares no deployment target in 'deployments', " +
              'so there is no store to run against. Declare a deployment in ' +
              "'deployments' whose target names a database.",
        });
  });

  // An empty list names no deployment, the same as no list.
  test('an empty deployments list gives no store to a named profile', () => {
    const emptyDeployments: SemanticModel = {...threeProfiles, deployments: []};
    expect(resolveStore(emptyDeployments, 'prod'))
        .toEqual({
          error: "binding profile 'prod' is a named profile, which names no " +
              'deployment target, so there is no database to run it against',
        });
  });

  // A legacy wrapper is merged into the model file, and push deploys it to
  // the model file's deployments when none names it.
  test('a legacy wrapper no deployment names takes the unprofiled ones', () => {
    const twoProfiles = deployed(
        `      - {name: bq_prod, target: "${BQ_GRAPH}", profile: analytical}\n` +
            `      - {name: spanner_prod, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n`,
        `${DB}/tables/Customer`);
    const store = resolveStore(twoProfiles, 'staging', {legacyWrapper: true});
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
    expect('error' in resolveStore(twoProfiles, 'staging')).toBe(true);
    // A deployment that names the wrapper is its own; this one is BigQuery.
    const analytical =
        resolveStore(twoProfiles, 'analytical', {legacyWrapper: true});
    expect('error' in analytical && analytical.error)
        .toContain('deployment target is projects/p/datasets/s');
  });

  // A blank `deployment_target` names no target, as push reads it, so the
  // loader makes no deployment of it.
  test('an empty deployment_target names no target', () => {
    for (const blank of ['""', '"   "']) {
      const store = resolveStore(
          model(
              `    deployment_target: ${blank}\n` +
              `    entities:\n` +
              `      - name: Customer\n` +
              `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
              `        fields:\n` +
              `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer}\n`),
          'prod', {legacyWrapper: true});
      expect(store).toEqual({
        error: expect.stringContaining('declares no deployment target'),
      });
    }
  });
});


// The loader keeps a Spanner or AlloyDB source written as a catalog name as
// it was written, and the store reads it.
describe('a catalog-name source', () => {
  function sourced(target: string, source: string): SemanticModel {
    return model(
        `    deployments:\n` +
        `      - {name: prod, target: "${target}"}\n` +
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        source: ${source}\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
  }

  const CLUSTER_DB =
      '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d';

  test('in Spanner matches a Spanner target', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(sourced(
        `${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`, 'spanner:p.regional-us-central1.i.d.Customer'));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.name).toBe('projects/p/instances/i/databases/d');
  });

  test('in AlloyDB matches an AlloyDB target', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(
        sourced(CLUSTER_DB, 'alloydb:p.us-central1.c.d.public.customer'));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
  });

  test('in another database is refused', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(sourced(
        CLUSTER_DB, 'alloydb:p.us-central1.c.other.public.customer'));
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain("'Customer' to alloydb:p.us-central1.c.other.public.customer");
  });
});


describe('an AlloyDB source', () => {
  const CLUSTER =
      '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c';

  function alloyModel(target: string, source: string): SemanticModel {
    return model(
        `    deployments:\n` +
        `      - {name: alloy_prod, target: "${target}"}\n` +
        `    entities:\n` +
        `      - name: Customer\n` +
        `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
        `        source: ${source}\n` +
        `        fields:\n` +
        `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
  }

  test('written as a table URI, matches a target with the same cluster and database',
       () => {
         const store = resolveStore(alloyModel(
             `${CLUSTER}/databases/d`,
             `${CLUSTER}/databases/d/schemas/public/tables/customer`));
         if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
         expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
       });

  test('in another database of the cluster is refused', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(alloyModel(
        `${CLUSTER}/databases/d`,
        `${CLUSTER}/databases/other/schemas/public/tables/customer`));
    expect('error' in store && store.error)
        .toContain("'Customer' to " + `${CLUSTER}/databases/other`);
  });

  // The instance is compute. The database belongs to the cluster, so a legacy
  // source's instance takes no part in the match.
  test('written as a legacy instance URI, matches on cluster and database', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(alloyModel(
        `${CLUSTER}/databases/d`,
        `${CLUSTER}/instances/any/databases/d/tables/customer`));
    if ('error' in store) throw new Error(store.error);
    expect(store.kind).toBe('alloydb');
  });
});


// A connection to an AlloyDB database goes through an instance, and a cluster
// target names none. The cluster's primary instance is the one to use.
describe('the instance an AlloyDB store connects through', () => {
  const CTX = new ApiContext('test-project', 'us', 'test-token');
  const CLUSTER = 'projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c';
  const store: AlloyDbDatabase = {
    kind: 'alloydb',
    name: `${CLUSTER}/databases/d`,
    project: 'p',
    location: 'us-central1',
    cluster: 'c',
    database: 'd',
  };

  function clientListing(result: api.ApiResult<Instance[]>): AlloyDbClient {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    spyOn(client, 'listInstances').mockResolvedValue(result);
    return client;
  }

  test('is the cluster\'s primary instance', async () => {
    const client = clientListing({
      status: 200,
      result: [
        {name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/reader`, instanceType: 'READ_POOL'},
        {
          name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/main`,
          instanceType: 'PRIMARY',
          state: 'READY',
        },
      ],
    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, client);
    if ('error' in found) throw new Error(found.error);
    expect(found.kind === 'alloydb' && found.instance).toBe('main');
    expect(storeLine(found)).toBe('alloydb:p/us-central1/c/main/d');
    expect(client.listInstances).toHaveBeenCalledWith('p', 'us-central1', 'c');
  });

  test('a cluster with no primary instance fails, naming the cluster',
       async () => {
         const found = await withPrimaryInstance(
             store, clientListing({
               status: 200,
               result: [{
                 name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/reader`,
                 instanceType: 'READ_POOL',
               }],
             }));
         expect('error' in found && found.error)
             .toBe(
                 `AlloyDB cluster '${CLUSTER}' has no primary instance, so ` +
                 `there is no instance to connect to database 'd' through.`);
       });

  test('a primary instance that is not READY fails, naming its state',
       async () => {
         const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, clientListing({
           status: 200,
           result: [{
             name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/main`,
             instanceType: 'PRIMARY',
             state: 'STOPPED',
           }],
         }));
         expect('error' in found && found.error)
             .toBe(
                 `AlloyDB cluster '${CLUSTER}' has primary instance 'main' in ` +
                 `state STOPPED; it must be READY to connect to database 'd' ` +
                 `through it.`);
       });

  test('a failed listing says why', async () => {
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, clientListing({
      status: 404,
      message: JSON.stringify(
          {error: {code: 404, message: "Resource 'clusters/c' was not found"}}),
    }));
    expect('error' in found && found.error)
        .toBe(
            `Could not list the instances of AlloyDB cluster '${CLUSTER}': ` +
            `404 Resource 'clusters/c' was not found`);
  });

  test('a listing that cannot be sent says why', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    spyOn(client, 'listInstances').mockRejectedValue(new Error('fetch failed'));
    expect(await withPrimaryInstance(store, client))
        .toEqual({
          error: `Could not list the instances of AlloyDB cluster '${
              CLUSTER}': fetch failed`,
        });
  });

  test('every page of the listing is read', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    const get = spyOn(client as any, '_get')
                    .mockResolvedValueOnce({
                      status: 200,
                      result: {
                        instances: [{
                          name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/reader`,
                          instanceType: 'READ_POOL',
                        }],
                        nextPageToken: 'T',
                      },
                    })
                    .mockResolvedValueOnce({
                      status: 200,
                      result: {
                        instances: [{
                          name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/main`,
                          instanceType: 'PRIMARY',
                          state: 'READY',
                        }],
                      },
                    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, client);
    if ('error' in found) throw new Error(found.error);
    expect(found.kind === 'alloydb' && found.instance).toBe('main');
    expect(get).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(get.mock.calls[0][0]).toBe(`${CLUSTER}/instances`);
    expect((get.mock.calls[1][1] as any).pageToken).toBe('T');
  });

  test('a failed page of the listing says why', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    spyOn(client as any, '_get')
        .mockResolvedValueOnce({
          status: 200,
          result: {
            instances: [
              {name: `${CLUSTER}/instances/reader`, instanceType: 'READ_POOL'},
            ],
            nextPageToken: 'T',
          },
        })
        .mockResolvedValueOnce({
          status: 403,
          message: JSON.stringify({error: {message: 'Permission denied'}}),
        });
    expect(await withPrimaryInstance(store, client))
        .toEqual({
          error: `Could not list the instances of AlloyDB cluster '${
              CLUSTER}': 403 Permission denied`,
        });
  });

  test('a listing that repeats a page token stops and says why', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    let calls = 0;
    // Gives up after ten pages, so a listing that does not stop fails here
    // and does not hang.
    spyOn(client as any, '_get').mockImplementation(async () => {
      calls++;
      return {
        status: 200,
        result: {
          instances: [],
          ...(calls < 10 ? {nextPageToken: 'same'} : {}),
        },
      };
    });
    expect(await withPrimaryInstance(store, client))
        .toEqual({
          error: `Could not list the instances of AlloyDB cluster '${
              CLUSTER}': the AlloyDB API returned page token 'same' twice`,
        });
    expect(calls).toBe(2);
  });

  test('a store that names its instance is not looked up', async () => {
    const client = clientListing({status: 500});
    const legacy = {...store, instance: 'i'};
    expect(await withPrimaryInstance(legacy, client)).toEqual(legacy);
    expect(client.listInstances).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

FILE: toolbox/mdcode/tests/libts/semantic/runtime/store_edge_cases.test.ts
================================================
// Edge cases for resolveStore and withPrimaryInstance: deployments that name
// profiles, targets push reads differently from a plain URI, and AlloyDB
// listings that page oddly. The AlloyDB listing is mocked.

import {describe, expect, spyOn, test} from 'bun:test';

import {AlloyDbClient} from '../../../../src/libts/gcp/alloydb';
import {ApiContext} from '../../../../src/libts/gcp/context';
import {resolveModelDeployments} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/deployment_target';
import {SemanticModel} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/ir';
import {loadModels} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/loader';
import {undeclaredProfileError} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/runtime';
import {AlloyDbDatabase, resolveStore, withPrimaryInstance} from '../../../../src/libts/semantic/runtime/store';

const DB = '//spanner.googleapis.com/projects/p/instances/i/databases/d';
const SPANNER_GRAPH = `${DB}/propertyGraphs/g`;
const CLUSTER =
    '//alloydb.googleapis.com/projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c';

function model(body: string): SemanticModel {
  return loadModels(
             `version: "0.2.0.dev0/google"\nsemantic_model:\n  - name: m\n${
                 body}`,
             {bindingOptional: true, allowLegacyBareSource: true})
      .models[0];
}

function deployed(entries: string, source = `${DB}/tables/Customer`):
    SemanticModel {
  return model(
      `    deployments:\n${entries}` +
      `    entities:\n` +
      `      - name: Customer\n` +
      `        primary_key: [id]\n` +
      `        source: ${source}\n` +
      `        fields:\n` +
      `          - {name: id, datatype: Integer, expression: id}\n`);
}

function vanilla(data: string): SemanticModel {
  return {
    ...deployed(`      - {name: x, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n`),
    version: '0.2.0.dev0',
    deployments: undefined,
    customExtensions: [{vendorName: 'GOOGLE', data}],
  };
}


describe('deployments and the profiles they name', () => {
  // `profile: default` names the model file's own bindings, so resolveStore
  // uses it for `default`, and so does a legacy wrapper that falls back to
  // those bindings.
  test('a deployment naming default is the model file\'s for a legacy wrapper too',
       () => {
         const m = deployed(
             `      - {name: prod, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}", profile: default}\n`);
         const byDefault = resolveStore(m, 'default');
         expect('error' in byDefault).toBe(false);
         const wrapped = resolveStore(m, 'staging', {legacyWrapper: true});
         expect(wrapped).toEqual(byDefault);
       });

  // A deployment whose profile no profile file declares would be used by no
  // profile. Push refuses the deployment, and so does the runtime.
  test('a deployment naming an undeclared profile is refused', () => {
    const m = deployed(
        `      - {name: prod, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}", profile: prdo}\n`);
    expect(undeclaredProfileError('m.yaml', m, ['prod']))
        .toBe(
            "[m.yaml] model 'm': deployment 'prod' names unknown binding " +
            "profile 'prdo'; defined profiles: prod.");
    expect(undeclaredProfileError('m.yaml', m, ['prdo'])).toBeUndefined();
  });

  // The legacy wrapper fallback uses the deployments for `default`, and the
  // ambiguity message says they are default's.
  test('the ambiguity message under a legacy wrapper names whose deployments they are',
       () => {
         const m = deployed(
             `      - {name: a, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n` +
             `      - {name: b, target: "${DB}2/propertyGraphs/g"}\n`);
         const store = resolveStore(m, 'staging', {legacyWrapper: true});
         expect('error' in store && store.error)
             .not.toContain("for profile 'staging' (a, b)");
         expect('error' in store && store.error)
             .toContain("in 'deployments' for profile 'default' (a, b)");
       });
});


describe('targets', () => {
  // A non-string entry is a target in no accepted form, to push and to the
  // runtime.
  test('a non-string GOOGLE block target fails the store', () => {
    const store = resolveStore(vanilla(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [42]})));
    expect(store).toEqual({
      error: expect.stringContaining('deploymentTargets'),
      named: true,
      rejected: true,
    });
  });

  // Push checks the target of every deployment a model declares, so a target
  // in no accepted form fails the store under every profile.
  test('a target in no accepted form for another profile fails the store',
       () => {
         const typo = `${DB}/propertyGraph/typo`;
         const m = deployed(
             `      - {name: dev, target: "${SPANNER_GRAPH}"}\n` +
             `      - {name: prod, target: "${typo}", profile: prod}\n`);
         expect(resolveStore(m, 'default')).toEqual({
           error: expect.stringContaining(`deployment 'prod' targets '${typo}'`),
           named: true,
           rejected: true,
         });
       });

  // So does a GOOGLE block that is not valid JSON, under a profile no
  // deployment uses.
  test('a GOOGLE block that is not valid JSON fails the store under every profile',
       () => {
         expect(resolveStore(vanilla('{not-json'), 'prod')).toEqual({
           error: "Model 'm': GOOGLE custom_extension 'data' is not valid JSON.",
           named: true,
           rejected: true,
         });
       });

  // Every push refuses a target listed twice. So does the runtime under every
  // profile, even beside a Spanner target that alone would give the store.
  test('a target a GOOGLE block lists twice fails the store under every profile',
       () => {
         const graph =
             '//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/p/datasets/d/propertyGraphs/g';
         const m = vanilla(
             JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [SPANNER_GRAPH, graph, graph]}));
         for (const profile of ['default', 'prod']) {
           expect(resolveStore(m, profile)).toEqual({
             error: `Model 'm' declares duplicate deployment target '${
                        graph}' in its GOOGLE block's 'deploymentTargets'; ` +
                 `each deployment must target a distinct resource.`,
             named: true,
             rejected: true,
           });
         }
       });

  // The instance-based AlloyDB URI in a `deployments:` list.
  // resolveModelDeployments rejects it, and resolveStore reads it until the
  // legacy forms go.
  test('an instance-based AlloyDB URI in a list: resolveStore reads it, resolveModelDeployments rejects it',
       () => {
         const m = deployed(
             `      - {name: old, target: "${CLUSTER}/instances/i/databases/d"}\n`,
             `${CLUSTER}/databases/d/schemas/public/tables/customer`);
         const store = resolveStore(m);
         expect('error' in store).toBe(false);
         expect('error' in resolveModelDeployments(m)).toBe(true);
       });

  // A programmatic empty list hides the GOOGLE block, the same way push
  // reads it, so both see no target.
  test('an empty deployments list beside a GOOGLE block reads no target', () => {
    const m: SemanticModel = {
      ...vanilla(JSON.stringify({deploymentTargets: [SPANNER_GRAPH]})),
      deployments: [],
    };
    const store = resolveStore(m);
    expect('error' in store && store.error).toContain('declares no deployment target');
  });
});


describe('the AlloyDB instance listing', () => {
  const CTX = new ApiContext('test-project', 'us', 'test-token');
  const store: AlloyDbDatabase = {
    kind: 'alloydb',
    name: 'projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c/databases/d',
    project: 'p',
    location: 'us-central1',
    cluster: 'c',
    database: 'd',
  };

  test('page tokens that cycle through two values stop', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    let calls = 0;
    spyOn(client as any, '_get').mockImplementation(async () => {
      calls++;
      return {
        status: 200,
        result: {instances: [], ...(calls < 10 ? {nextPageToken: calls % 2 ? 'A' : 'B'} : {})},
      };
    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, client);
    expect('error' in found && found.error).toContain("page token 'A' twice");
    expect(calls).toBe(3);
  });

  test('a primary with no name is reported as missing', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    spyOn(client, 'listInstances').mockResolvedValue({
      status: 200,
      result: [{instanceType: 'PRIMARY', state: 'READY'}],
    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, client);
    expect('error' in found && found.error).toContain('has no primary instance');
  });

  test('a listing page that is not a list fails, naming the cluster', async () => {
    const client = new AlloyDbClient(CTX);
    spyOn(client as any, '_get').mockResolvedValue({
      status: 200,
      result: {instances: {name: 'x'}},
    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, client);
    expect('error' in found && found.error)
        .toContain("Could not list the instances of AlloyDB cluster 'projects/p/locations/us-central1/clusters/c'");
  });

  test('a token that cannot be read fails, naming the cluster', async () => {
    const ctx = new ApiContext('test-project', 'us', 'test-token');
    Object.defineProperty(ctx, 'token', {
      get() {
        throw new Error('gcloud is not installed');
      },
    });
    const found = await withPrimaryInstance(store, new AlloyDbClient(ctx));
    expect('error' in found && found.error)
        .toContain('gcloud is not installed');
  });
});

name: pull_basic
description: EntryGroup with single entry
setup:
  catalog:
    entryGroups:
      - name: projects/test/locations/us/entryGroups/g1
    entryTypes:
      - name: projects/test/locations/global/entryTypes/et1
    entries:
      - name: projects/test/locations/us/entryGroups/g1/entries/e1
        entryType: projects/test/locations/global/entryTypes/et1

  fileSystem:
    catalog.yaml: |
      scope: entryGroup.test.us.g1

actions:
  - action: pull

assert:

name: pull_parent_entry
description: >
  A pulled entry with a parentEntry writes the parent into the local snapshot so
  it round-trips (regression: toLocalEntry used to drop parentEntry).
setup:
  catalog:
    entryGroups:
      - name: projects/test/locations/us/entryGroups/g1
    entryTypes:
      - name: projects/test/locations/global/entryTypes/et1
    entries:
      - name: projects/test/locations/us/entryGroups/g1/entries/child
        entryType: projects/test/locations/global/entryTypes/et1
        parentEntry: projects/test/locations/us/entryGroups/g1/entries/parent

  fileSystem:
    catalog.yaml: |
      scope: entryGroup.test.us.g1

actions:
  - action: pull

assert:
  fileSystem:
    catalog/child.yaml:
      - contains: "name: child"
      # Stored as a bare local name (not the service name), matching how a
      # human authors an entry and how _fetchEntry re-derives it on push.
      - contains: "parent: parent"

      - name: projects/p/locations/global/aspectTypes/aspect1
      - name: projects/p/locations/global/aspectTypes/aspect2
    entries:
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/custom-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old custom description
        aspects:
          p.global.aspect1:
            aspectType: projects/p/locations/global/aspectTypes/aspect1
            data:
              content: Old aspect1
          p.global.aspect2:
            aspectType: projects/p/locations/global/aspectTypes/aspect2
            data:
              content: Old aspect2
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/other-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/other-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old other description

  fileSystem:
    catalog.yaml: |
      scope: entryGroup.p.us.custom-group
      snapshot:
        entries:
          - p.global.custom-type
          - p.global.other-type
        aspects:
          - p.global.aspect1
          - p.global.aspect2
      publishing:
        entries:
          - p.global.custom-type
        aspects:
          - p.global.aspect1

              content: New aspect1

name: push_validate_only_create
description: >
  A --validate-only push that would create a new entry writes nothing to the
  catalog (regression for the ignored validateOnly flag on non-semantic scopes).
setup:
  catalog:
    entryGroups:
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group
    entryTypes:
      - name: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
    entries:
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/existing-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old custom description

  fileSystem:
    catalog.yaml: |
      scope: entryGroup.p.us.custom-group
      snapshot:
        entries:
          - p.global.custom-type

actions:
  - action: pull
  - action: createEntry
    name: custom-entry
    entry:
      name: custom-entry
      type: p.global.custom-type
      resource:
        description: Hello world
  - action: push
    options:
      validateOnly: true

assert:
  # The local snapshot still holds the staged entry ...
  fileSystem:
    catalog/custom-entry.yaml:
      - contains: "name: custom-entry"
      - contains: "description: Hello world"
  # ... but the catalog is untouched: no new entry was created.
  catalog:
    entries:
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/existing-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old custom description

      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/custom-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old custom description

  fileSystem:
    catalog.yaml: |
      scope: entryGroup.p.us.custom-group
      snapshot:
        entries:
          - p.global.custom-type

actions:
  - action: pull
  - action: updateEntry
    entry:
      name: custom-entry
      type: p.global.custom-type
      resource:
        description: New custom description
    fields:
      - resource
  - action: push
    options:
      validateOnly: true

assert:
  # The local snapshot holds the edited description ...
  fileSystem:
    catalog/custom-entry.yaml:
      - contains: "name: custom-entry"
      - contains: "description: New custom description"
  # ... but the catalog still shows the old description: nothing was modified.
  catalog:
    entries:
      - name: projects/p/locations/us/entryGroups/custom-group/entries/custom-entry
        entryType: projects/p/locations/global/entryTypes/custom-type
        entrySource:
          description: Old custom description

describe('push prints Knowledge Catalog warnings', () => {
  const RESULT = {
    success: true, created: 1, updated: 0, deleted: 0, linked: 0, unlinked: 0,
    warnings: ['a relationship is skipped'], plan: [],
  };
  // The model binds no table and declares no named profile, so push warns
  // before it reaches the catalog.
  const NON_EXECUTABLE = "Warning: model 'commerce' (commerce) is " +
      "non-executable: the model file leaves entity 'Customer' without a " +
      'source, and the model declares no named profile. It cannot be ' +
      'queried until it is bound.';

  test('before the first catalog write, once each', async () => {
    writeWorkspace();
    const events: string[] = [];
    spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation((m: any) => {
      events.push(String(m));
    });
    spyOn(kc, 'deployKnowledgeCatalog')
        .mockImplementation(async (_models, _ctx, opts) => {
          opts.onWarnings?.(RESULT.warnings);
          events.push('first catalog write');
          return RESULT;
        });

    expect(await push({})).toBe(0);
    expect(events).toEqual([
      NON_EXECUTABLE,
      'Warning: a relationship is skipped',
      'first catalog write',
    ]);
  });

  test('under --validate-only, from the result', async () => {
    writeWorkspace();
    const warn = spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
    spyOn(kc, 'deployKnowledgeCatalog').mockResolvedValue(RESULT);

    expect(await push({validateOnly: true})).toBe(0);
    expect(warn.mock.calls.map(c => String(c[0]))).toEqual([
      NON_EXECUTABLE,
      'Warning: a relationship is skipped',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('a push with a sibling profile file', () => {
  test('a graph push of the profile file is refused before anything deploys', async () => {
    fs.writeFileSync(
        path.join(dir, 'catalog.yaml'),
        'scope: semantic-model.test-project.us.commerce_eg\n');
    const eg = path.join(dir, 'catalog', 'EntryGroups', 'commerce_eg');
